papers.title: FUNATOMY: Exploring Student Perceptions of Low-Cost Game-Based Learning in First-Year Anatomy
papers.abstract: Background: Game-based learning (GBL) is increasingly used in anatomy education to promote active learning; however, little is known about students’ perceptions of multiple low-cost GBL activities embedded in routine anatomy practicals. This study explored first-year health sciences students’ perceptions of the benefits and limitations of FUNATOMY, low-cost GBL activities integrated into anatomy practical sessions. Methods: A qualitative exploratory study was conducted among first-year students in four health sciences programs at the University of Pretoria, South Africa. Written reflections from 200 consenting students were analyzed using an AI-assisted inductive thematic approach. Two large language models were used as exploratory tools to generate preliminary themes that informed subsequent researcher-led thematic analysis. Two researchers independently assigned themes to student responses, resolving discrepancies through discussion and consensus. Results: Eight themes were established: Enjoyment; Understanding and application; Memory and knowledge retention; Learning environment; Collaboration; Complementary learning strategy; Knowledge gaps; and Did not help. Students described the activities as enjoyable and engaging and felt they supported retrieval and reinforcement of previously learned knowledge, understanding and application, collaboration, and recognition of knowledge gaps. Students viewed FUNATOMY as complementary to, rather than a replacement for, specimen-based anatomy practical teaching. Conclusions: The findings reflect students’ perceptions of FUNATOMY and suggest that the activities were viewed as a useful supplement to traditional anatomy practicals. However, the study did not objectively assess learning outcomes or establish the activities’ effectiveness.

papers.title: Active learning in a large calculus class improves student satisfaction and performance
papers.abstract: Active learning strategies during large lectures promote student activity and are known to improve student performance and engagement. In this work, an array of cognitive-science-based and psychological active learning strategies are introduced in large lectures in a first-year undergraduate course in single-variable calculus and analytical geometry. The implemented active learning strategies correspond to preclass quizzes and in-class problem solving followed by student-student discussion using Mentimeter, demonstrations avoiding the curse of knowledge and giving context before content, a popular science-style inspiration lecture, promoting cycles of positivity in teaching and the use of motivational nudges. To evaluate the efficiency of these active learning strategies, the satisfaction and performance of the students engaged in active learning are compared to students attending traditional lectures in the same calculus course during the previous two years. Diagnostic tests before the calculus course reveal that the prerequisite skills of the students of all years are similar. The final grades in the course based on final test scores and grades given by students in course surveys after the course reveal that active learning strategies improve student performance and satisfaction compared to traditional lectures. In addition, the students engaged in active learning greatly enjoyed the active learning strategies implemented and reported high levels of motivation and psychological safety in the course survey. Together with other studies, this work cements the efficiency of active learning strategies and provides practical guidance on how these strategies can be implemented.

papers.title: Schrödinger's Cat Revisited: The De-Scalarization of Mathematical Physics (A Unified World Model)
papers.abstract: This work develops a relational framework in which particles, fields, forces, composite systems, thermodynamic states, cosmological observables, and measurement records are treated as typed publications of a single reversible real carrier rather than as hierarchically distinct layers of reality. The central construction is a continuous, peak-anchored publication geometry in which gravitational, color, electroweak, and electromagnetic structures remain equal-status realizations of one twisted carrier while their observable weights and resolutions change with publication depth. The framework is built on real finite-order carrier structures and develops Lorentz, Clifford, gauge, electromagnetic, gravitational, fermionic, hadronic, nuclear, atomic, quantum, thermodynamic, and cosmological realizations without taking complex scalar structure as primitive. Electroweak and Higgs responses close through the neutral peak, while a common vacuum carrier relates the Higgs and gravitational vacuum publications without requiring isolated particle poles or a completed fermion mass spectrum. Quantum measurement, decoherence, entropy production, thermality, recombination, optical visibility, and cosmological observation arise as increasingly terminal publications rather than as fundamental irreversible dynamics. Dark matter is correspondingly interpreted as the exclusively or predominantly gravitationally published part of the terminal observable structure whose ordinary electromagnetic publication has become suppressed, while the cosmic microwave background is the last resolved optical screen rather than an asserted boundary of the complete carrier.

papers.title: Machine Learning on Small Experimental Datasets in Manufacturing: A Review of Data Leakage, Grouped Validation, and Uncertainty Quantification
papers.abstract: Machine learning is increasingly used to predict machining and process quality from experimental data, yet such data are typically small, generated by designed experiments, and hierarchically organized, with several measurements taken on the same specimen, tool, or batch. Under these conditions, standard evaluation practice can substantially overstate predictive performance. This review synthesizes the methodological literature from statistics, machine learning, and applied domains to provide guidance for small-data machine learning in manufacturing. We present a taxonomy of data-leakage pathways, compare validation strategies (row-wise, grouped, blocked, nested, and bootstrap-based), discuss model families suited to small tabular data, and review uncertainty-quantification methods, including conformal prediction for grouped data and statistical procedures for comparing models. A reproducible simulation of a specimen–section design shows that row-wise cross-validation increasingly underestimates the error on new specimens as within-specimen correlation grows—whereas grouped cross-validation remains close to it—and that non-nested model selection yields optimistic estimates. Additional experiments with constant total variance, a full-factorial design, and six model families show that the bias is driven by within-specimen dependence and is largest for flexible learners. The review concludes with a reporting checklist and open research directions.

papers.title: Comparative PECS and LPBF Processing of Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3: Microstructure, Texture, and Thermoelectric Performance
papers.abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) is emerging as a promising manufacturing route for next-generation thermoelectric generators, offering unprecedented freedom in the fabrication of complex device geometries. However, the rapid melting and solidification inherent to LPBF produce microstructures fundamentally different from those of conventional consolidation techniques, and how these processing-induced features affect thermoelectric performance remains poorly understood. In this work, LPBF-produced p-type Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3 was compared with materials fabricated by pulsed electric current sintering (PECS), which served as a reference processing route providing a higher degree of crystallographic texture. The comparison enabled identification of the microstructural characteristics governing electrical and thermal transport. In particular, the investigated materials exhibited a wide range of preferred orientation (Lotgering factor F ≈ 0.02-0.20), while maintaining comparable Seebeck coefficients (∼160-175 μV K-1). In contrast, electrical conductivity (720-2200 S cm-1 at 300 K), thermal conductivity (0.9-1.5 W m-1 K-1), and consequently the thermoelectric figure of merit varied strongly with the processing route and crystallographic orientation. PECS samples with moderate preferred orientation reached ZT ≈ 1.1, while LPBF specimens exhibited ZT ≈ 0.4-0.5. The lower LPBF performance reflects weaker texture and processing-induced defects, partly related to nonideal powder morphology and feeding conditions. Additionally, numerical modeling (FEM) was performed to evaluate energy conversion efficiency, demonstrating higher output power and overall efficiency for the PECS samples compared to the LPBF ones. The comparative analysis demonstrates that crystallographic texture and microstructural integrity are key factors affecting thermoelectric performance and identifies processing-related limitations under the LPBF conditions investigated in this study.

To address this, we propose a two-stage framework in which a digital twin, a Gaussian process trained on 600 observations from 30 simulated patients, warm-starts Bayesian optimization for a new patient. In simulation, the twin reached a near-best setting in a median of 1 trial, compared with 6 for random search and 4 for tuned Bayesian optimization (90 runs per method). In our additional analyses, we found that the benefit comes mainly from the pretrained prior and not from tailoring to injury severity, that it is robust to parameter changes but weaker when the response landscape changes, and that the model’s gait rhythm is 16.2 percent slower than that of ten healthy adults from a public database. This is a simulation study, and we propose calibration with real EES patient data and a small clinician pilot as the next step.

papers.title: An Method of Assessing Lithium-Ion Battery State of Health Based on Interval Belief Rule Base
papers.abstract: The accurate assessment of lithium-ion battery State of Health (SOH) is fundamental to the safe and reliable operation of battery management systems. The Belief Rule Base (BRB) integrates quantitative monitoring data and qualitative expert knowledge, thereby supporting SOH assessment. However, existing BRB models produce point-value outputs. The uncertainty of the assessment results cannot be quantified, nor can the belief level of the assessment be characterized. Moreover, information loss is caused by traditional evidential reasoning (ER) when interval belief degrees are processed. Interval reliability is not adequately addressed in existing optimization methods, as interval quality is not incorporated into the objective function. To address these problems, an interval SOH assessment method based on the Interval Belief Rule Base with Interval Evidential Reasoning (IBRB-IER) is proposed. Rule belief degrees are extended from point values to interval forms, enabling uncertainty quantification. Interval information is preserved throughout the fusion process by adopting interval evidential reasoning algorithms. A multi-objective composite fitness function is designed. Global parameter optimization is achieved through the projected covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (P-CMA-ES). SOH estimation intervals are finally produced as outputs. The effectiveness of the proposed method in SOH interval assessment is validated through experiments on the NASA dataset.

papers.title: A Web-Based Interface and Machine Learning for Intelligent Stroke Risk Assessment
papers.abstract: Abstract— Early identification of people with common, easily available health markers that indicate a pattern of higher risk is helpful to prevent stroke. We have developed a ML screening method for brain-stroke vulnerability using structured demographical, clinical and lifestyle data which is available via the web. The proposed method is based on the EBM along with the Mondrian CP and SA. LR, DT, KNN and Gaussian NB are used as baseline classifiers. The EBM is trained to learn additive feature functions that are interpretable and the conformal layer generates prediction sets output for each class with a desired coverage target. If the circumstances are ambiguous, no attempt to label them as risky is made, but instead the interface provides a Review Required state. Experimental results of the EBM point classifier produce results of 94.7% accuracy, 92.8% precision, 95.9% recall, 94.3% F1-score and 97.1% ROC-AUC. The proposed uncertainty layer has an empirical coverage of 90.8% at nominal conformal coverage level of 90% and an abstention rate of 8.6%. The final architecture represents an interpretable and uncertainty-aware web screening approach that relies on intrinsic additive modelling and uncertainty in the prediction set. “Index Terms—stroke prediction, machine learning, Explainable Boosting Machine, conformal prediction, selective prediction, web application, uncertainty-aware screening.”

papers.title: Uncertainty-aware determination of thermal transmittance and systematic evaluation of insulation retrofit scenarios for energy-efficient building envelope
papers.abstract: Abstract Thermal transmittance (U-value) assessment is essential for improving energy efficiency in buildings, particularly under real operating conditions where transient heat transfer and measurement uncertainties affect reliability. This study proposes a novel framework that combines non-intrusive infrared thermography, uncertainty quantification based on the Guide to the Expression of Uncertainty in Measurement (GUM), and dynamic heat transfer analysis for in-situ U-value estimation. The objectives are to evaluate and compare instantaneous, smoothing, and Cumulative Time-Integrated approaches and support the systematic assessment of insulation retrofit strategies. The proposed methods are applied to the external wall of a single-family house in Brazil, characterized by a warm and humid climate classification. In-situ measurements of indoor and outdoor air temperatures and surface temperature are used to estimate heat flux through convective heat-transfer modeling. Uncertainty propagation is incorporated using sensitivity coefficients, enabling a rigorous evaluation of the influence of measurement errors and environmental variability on U-value estimation. The framework is extended to analyze retrofit scenarios using insulation materials, including expanded polystyrene (EPS) and extruded polystyrene (XPS), combined with internal and external covering layers such as gypsum board and acrylic render. The results show that instantaneous U-values are highly sensitive to transient conditions and low temperature gradients, while smoothing improves stability but may introduce bias. The Cumulative U-value provides the most robust and physically representative estimate. Retrofit analysis indicates that insulation layers significantly reduce thermal transmittance, with external systems performing better under solar exposure and internal configurations enhancing indoor thermal stability. The study supports effective energy-efficiency interventions in building envelopes.

papers.title: A reinforcement learning-enhanced collision avoidance strategy integrating motion planning and control
papers.abstract: Existing automotive collision avoidance (CA) systems typically adopt a multi-layer architecture, separating motion planning and control due to computational complexity and differing optimization horizons, leading to potential conflicts and compromised safety in complex collision avoidance scenarios. To this end, this paper proposes a novel reinforcement learning-enhanced CA strategy that integrates motion planning and control processes. A cascaded nonlinear model predictive control (CNMPC) approach is proposed, employing high-fidelity nonlinear dynamics for immediate control actions and simplified linear dynamics for long-term trajectory planning. Additionally, a horizon-decreasing risk-weighting (HDRW) strategy is introduced to prioritize imminent collision risks, addressing the limitations of traditional model predictive control (MPC) in multi-obstacle situations. Furthermore, reinforcement learning (RL)-based adaptive control agents are developed to dynamically adjust the coordination strategy between the longitudinal and lateral inputs based on real-time road adhesion, enhancing the system’s environmental adaptability and robustness. Simulations and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) experiments under multi-obstacle CA scenarios with low and varying road adhesion demonstrate the proposed strategy’s feasibility and superior performance, ensuring safe and stable collision avoidance under complex road conditions.

papers.title: Synergistic Effects of Carbon/Nitrogen Content and Laser Powder Bed Fusion Parameters on the Hot Cracking Behavior and Microstructural Evolution of a Ni–Co‐Based Superalloy
papers.abstract: The broad industrial adoption of additively manufactured superalloys is severely hindered by hot cracking. This research utilizes laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) to provide a systematic elucidation of how carbon and nitrogen concentrations interact with processing conditions to govern the microstructural development and crack initiation mechanisms within a Ni–Co‐based superalloy. With increasing carbon and nitrogen content, the areal fraction of intergranular carbides increases markedly. Meanwhile, the carbides decorating grain boundaries transition from discrete particles to quasi‐continuous and ultimately continuous networks, accompanied by enhanced nitride precipitation. These hard and brittle phases refine the cellular solidification structure but substantially increase the proportion of high‐angle grain boundaries (HAGBs). Their pronounced pinning effect hinders liquid feeding during the terminal stage of solidification, thereby creating preferential crack‐initiation sites and accelerating intergranular crack propagation. Furthermore, increasing the energy density and laser power significantly heightens crack susceptibility by modifying molten‐pool thermodynamics and intensifying thermal stress gradients, whereas an appropriately optimized processing window effectively suppresses crack formation. Overall, this study establishes mechanistic and quantitative linkages among alloy chemistry, LPBF‐induced microstructural features, and hot‐cracking behavior, thereby providing a rigorous scientific foundation for the composition design and process optimization of LPBF‐fabricated superalloys.

papers.title: Stochastic Mortality Modelling for Small and Data-Scarce Populations: A Systematic Literature Review
papers.abstract: Stochastic mortality models developed for large national populations face challenges when applied to small populations with volatile death counts, short data series, and potentially biased parameter estimates. This systematic review synthesizes modelling strategies for small and data-scarce populations from an actuarial perspective, examining uncertainty quantification, model evaluation, and remaining research gaps. Following PRISMA 2020, records were identified through Semantic Scholar and citation snowballing. Of 40 unique records screened, 18 studies published between 2011 and 2026 met the eligibility criteria; included journal articles appeared in Scopus-indexed journals. Data were extracted using a structured form and synthesized thematically. Five categories emerged: reference-population and two-population models, credibility and Bayesian methods, analyses of small-population bias, subnational and small-area methods, and hybrids incorporating machine learning. Most approaches stabilized projections by borrowing information from larger, related populations. However, the reviewed machine-learning studies seldom reported forecast intervals, and none of the included studies used Southeast Asian data. The evidence supports selecting an appropriate reference population and reporting distinct sources of uncertainty separately when modelling mortality in small populations. By consolidating these approaches and their limitations, the review clarifies the methodological foundations of small-population mortality modelling and provides practical guidance for actuaries in data-scarce markets, including Indonesia. It also identifies uncertainty reporting and Southeast Asian applications as priorities for further research.

papers.title: Ǝnuoχ · Iïraŋ: The Optimal Frequency Cost of Quantum Haar Ergodicity-Exact Quasiperiodic Constructions, Smooth Bounded Approximation, and Regularity Obstructions
papers.abstract: This research release presents analytical constructions, obstruction theorems, and reproducible numerical checks for quantum Haar ergodicity in finite-dimensional driven systems. Its central question is how many independent external base frequencies are required for a deterministic quantum evolution to reproduce Haar-distributed unitary behavior in the long-time limit. The manuscript derives the count m = d(d − 1) for every Hilbert-space dimension d ≥ 2 within its stated regular quasienergy-reducible setting. This is a conditional optimality statement about a specified class of dynamics. The construction addresses the gap between the d² − 2 sufficient construction and the d² − d conditional lower bound discussed in Pilatowsky-Cameo, Marvian, Choi, and Ho, “Hilbert-Space Ergodicity in Driven Quantum Systems: Obstructions and Designs,” Physical Review X 14, 041059 (2024), DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevX.14.041059. Established Haar-coordinate methods, including the work of Spengler, Huber, and Hiesmayr, are credited explicitly. The proposed contribution is their use in a frequency-optimal dynamical construction, together with approximation and obstruction results. PureOne/Enuokh-Iirang-Optimal-Quantum-Haar-Ergodicity · Datasets at Hugging Face The main results are: Exact construction at the conditional minimum. A recursive special-unitary flag map uses d(d − 1)/2 radial coordinates and the same number of phase coordinates. All d − 1 independent diagonal angles are supplied by quasienergy evolution rather than additional external drive frequencies. Joint rational independence gives a Haar SU(d) long-time limiting law. Its balanced unitary moments and projective unitary channels agree with those of Haar U(d); the construction does not generate an independent random global U(1) phase. The exact control has integrable, unbounded cusp peaks, an absolutely continuous propagator, and finite action on every finite interval. Finite action does not generally imply finite squared-amplitude power. Smooth bounded approximation at the same frequency count. For any prescribed 0 < ε < 1, radial truncation and smooth convolution yield globally C∞, uniformly bounded controls whose long-time limiting law lies within total variation ε of Haar. Consequently, every finite-order parallel unitary twirl has limiting half-diamond error at most ε, and every initial pure state satisfies the corresponding limiting moment bound. The guarantee is uniform over moment order after taking the infinite-time limit separately at each fixed order. It supplies no finite-time estimate uniform over all orders. A matching all-order lower bound. Under the manuscript’s regular quasienergy assumptions, using fewer than d(d − 1) external base frequencies forces the supremum of the limiting all-order half-diamond errors to equal one. The argument combines a dimension obstruction with a tomography-based relation between tensor-power moments and total variation. Together with the smooth construction, this identifies the same minimum count for uniform all-order limiting error strictly below one in the declared class. A global regularity obstruction. Exact complete unitary ergodicity with globally C¹ quasienergy micromotion requires m ≥ d(d − 1) + 1. The corresponding state-ray result requires m ≥ 2d − 1. These are necessary bounds; sufficiency at the raised counts is not proved. Their hypotheses concern the global regularity of quasienergy functions, rather than smoothness of the physical Hamiltonian alone. They therefore do not establish that every exact physical realization must use unbounded controls. Complementary temporal-window and measurement results. Part II retains a sharp frontier relating projector-population variance to second-moment deviation, a macroscopic-window obstruction to Haar second-moment ergodicity, a no-go theorem for the substitution drive 0 → 010, 1 → 111, and a finite two-copy measurement certificate. The variance concerns fluctuations of expectation values across states or times, rather than the measurement variance within one state. The two-copy certificate assumes independently prepared copies evaluated at the same uniformly selected time. The generic critical substitution 0 → 001, 1 → 11 remains unresolved. The release includes the final manuscript, LaTeX source, analytical derivations, a reusable Python generator, scientific figures, numerical ledgers, fixed-seed verification scripts, reproduction instructions, and internal proof-audit records. The core generator supports the exact cusp construction and a bounded piecewise-smooth truncation. A separate adaptive-quadrature prototype checks the globally C∞ construction; it is not an exact digital representation of the analytic smoothing kernel. Recorded checks include 9,000 SU(d) map cases in dimensions 2–10; 200,000 torus samples compared with 200,000 independent QR-Haar samples; low-order state and balanced unitary moments; 150 analytic-derivative checks; 1,500 bounded-Hamiltonian norm samples; six direct ODE intervals; eight finite-action quadratures; and 12 finite quasiperiodic moment windows. The smooth prototype adds 670 profile and derivative checks, ten error-budget configurations, 101 Hamiltonian samples, and an ODE interval crossing a cusp. These computations test ideal mathematical models. Exactness, all-order statements, and infinite-time conclusions rest on the analytical arguments rather than finite numerical sampling. Scope and research status: frequency count means independent base-frequency rank, not the number of Fourier harmonics, pure sinusoidal controls, hardware channels, or gates. No finite-bandwidth guarantee, efficient many-qubit scaling, or quantitative mixing-time advantage is established. The lower bounds do not cover arbitrary irreducible quantum dynamics. Internal agent audits are not external peer review or proof-assistant certification, and the release contains no experimental hardware validation. Worldwide priority remains unconfirmed. papers.title: Machine Learning for Predictive Maintenance of Industrial Systems: A Review of Methods, Benchmarks, Challenges and Future Directions
papers.abstract: Aims: To critically review how machine learning is applied to predictive maintenance of industrial assets, to compare the main method families and benchmark practices, and to identify the barriers that limit industrial adoption and the priorities for future research. Study Design: Narrative (non-systematic) review. Methodology: Peer-reviewed journal articles, conference papers and established review studies published between 2006 and 2026 were identified from major scientific databases and publisher platforms using combinations of the terms predictive maintenance, condition monitoring, fault diagnosis, prognostics, remaining useful life and machine learning. Seminal and highly cited works, benchmark-dataset papers and recent advances were prioritised. The evidence was synthesised by maintenance task, method family, dataset, evaluation metric and deployment issue. Results: Machine learning in predictive maintenance has progressed from feature-engineered shallow classifiers to deep convolutional, recurrent and attention-based networks that learn directly from raw sensor signals, and, more recently, to transfer learning, federated learning, physics-informed hybrid models and large foundation models. Deep models report strong accuracy on public benchmarks for bearing fault diagnosis and turbofan remaining-useful-life estimation, and hybrid physics and deep-learning models have extended prognostic horizons while requiring less training data. However, most evidence comes from a small number of laboratory or simulated datasets; performance under domain shift, scarce failure data, uncertainty quantification, interpretability and the link between prediction and maintenance decisions remain weakly addressed. Conclusion: Machine learning is a mature enabler of predictive maintenance, but industrial value depends less on marginal benchmark gains than on robust, explainable, uncertainty-aware and decision-oriented models validated on field data. Standardised evaluation protocols, open industrial datasets, hybrid knowledge-and-data models and cost-benefit evidence are the main priorities for future work.

papers.title: An Explainable and Optimized Ensemble Learning Framework Using XGBoost, CatBoost, and LightGBM for Tabular Predictive Analytics
papers.abstract: This study presents an explainable and Bayesian-optimized stacking ensemble learning framework for predictive analytics on complex tabular datasets. The proposed framework integrates XGBoost, CatBoost, and LightGBM as heterogeneous base learners, with hyperparameters optimized using Tree-Structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) Bayesian optimization through Optuna. To reduce validation bias and data leakage, the framework employs nested stratified five-fold cross-validation and constructs an out-of-fold probability matrix for an ElasticNet-regularized logistic meta-learner. The framework is evaluated using the UCI Default of Credit Card Clients dataset containing 30,000 records and 23 input variables. On an independent holdout test set of 6,000 observations, the proposed stacking meta-ensemble achieved an accuracy of 82.41%, F1-score of 0.4924, PR-AUC of 0.5612, and ROC-AUC of 0.7891. Statistical evaluation using DeLong's test, the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and bootstrap confidence intervals indicates that the ensemble provides a statistically significant improvement over the strongest individual learner, CatBoost. Model transparency is provided through TreeSHAP, enabling global feature-importance analysis and local instance-level explanations. The results demonstrate a practical trade-off between predictive performance, interpretability, and computational efficiency for high-stakes tabular predictive analytics.

papers.title: From Conventional Image Processing to Artificial Intelligence in Electron Microscopy: Toward Robust, Automated, and Enhanced Materials Characterization Through Insights from Medical and Biological Imaging
papers.abstract: Electron microscopy is fundamental to modern materials characterization; however, the quantitative analysis of scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) data remains challenged by noise, imaging artifacts, acquisition variability, complex microstructures, and operator-dependent interpretation. This review examines the evolution of computational analysis from conventional image-processing techniques, including filtering, deconvolution, enhancement, and segmentation, toward machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) approaches for electron microscopy. Particular attention is given to convolutional and generative architectures, self-supervised learning, transfer learning and domain adaptation, transformers and foundation models, physics-informed learning, and multimodal integration of imaging, spectroscopic, diffraction, and three-dimensional data. Advances in medical and biological imaging are further examined to identify transferable strategies for data-efficient learning, image reconstruction, multimodal analysis, uncertainty quantification, and external validation. Collectively, these developments indicate a transition from task-specific image processing toward increasingly integrated, automated, and quantitative characterization workflows. Nevertheless, limited datasets, domain shifts across instruments and material classes, computational demands, physical consistency, and insufficient standardization remain major challenges. Future advances will require robust, generalizable, and physically informed artificial intelligence frameworks capable of integrating heterogeneous microscopy data while maintaining scientific interpretability and reliability.

papers.title: Hybrid modeling and control of stress-dependent tumor evolution under pathway-targeted therapies
papers.abstract: Targeted therapies suppress tumor growth by inhibiting specific oncogenic signaling pathways. However, sustained inhibition perturbs intracellular signaling and exerts selective stress on cancer cells, triggering compensatory responses that alter proliferation, survival, and drug sensitivity. To capture these mechanisms in a tractable, control-oriented framework, we propose a hybrid model in which stress-induced changes in cellular phenotype and treatment response are represented through state-dependent parameter switching and absorbing dynamics. Tumor growth is described by a proliferating cell population coupled to adaptive traits representing the activity and interactions of three key pathways: Wnt/ β -catenin, PI3K/Akt, and MAPK/ERK. Trait evolution captures reversible stress-induced plasticity, while sustained stress triggers discrete parameter updates and, upon saturation, absorbing states associated with irreversible resistance and loss of therapeutic efficacy. Baseline parameters are calibrated using in vivo xenograft data under pathway-specific inhibition. We then propose a hybrid model predictive control strategy with a supervisory layer that adapts therapy to the current discrete mode and selectively suspends treatment on critical pathways. Numerical simulations show the dual benefit of the framework, which preserves modeling tractability while enabling policies that prevent resistance.

papers.title: Microphysiological Systems for Musculoskeletal Research: Current Advances in Organ-on-Chip Platforms
papers.abstract: Organ-on-chip (OoC) technology has emerged as a powerful class of microphysiological systems capable of recapitulating human tissue architecture, biochemical gradients, and dynamic cellular interactions with high fidelity. While OoC platforms have advanced rapidly in organs such as liver, heart, and lung, their application to the musculoskeletal system remains comparatively underdeveloped despite the central role of biomechanics in tissue function and disease. Musculoskeletal tissues, including skeletal muscle, bone, cartilage, and tendon, present unique challenges due to their hierarchical structure, anisotropic mechanical properties, and tightly coupled immune, vascular, and stromal interactions that govern repair and degeneration. In this review, we critically evaluate recent advances in musculoskeletal OoC platforms, including muscle, bone, cartilage, and tendon-on-chip systems, with emphasis on structural design, biomaterial composition, and integration of mechanical cues. We highlight how these systems enable precise control of microenvironmental conditions and support human-relevant disease modeling and drug testing. However, we identify key limitations that constrain their translational potential, including inadequate representation of physiologically relevant mechanical loading, incomplete vascular and immune integration, lack of standardization, and limited modeling of inter-tissue interfaces. Importantly, we propose a unifying framework for next-generation musculoskeletal OoC systems centered on three principles: mechanobiological fidelity, multicellular integration, and interface-level modeling of the muscle–tendon–bone axis. We further discuss emerging strategies, including advanced biomaterials, 3D bioprinting, multi-tissue integration, and artificial-intelligence-driven analysis that can address current limitations and enable scalable, predictive platforms. By bridging reductionist in vitro systems and complex in vivo physiology, musculoskeletal OoC technologies have the potential to transform mechanobiology research, accelerate drug discovery, and enable precision regenerative therapies. Realizing this potential will require coordinated advances in engineering, biology, and standardization to establish OoC platforms as robust, clinically relevant tools for musculoskeletal medicine.

papers.title: Energy-absorbing metamaterials based on DNA helices
papers.abstract: The increasing demand for vehicle safety creates a need to develop of efficient protective systems with enhanced energy absorption performance. The results of the development and investigation of energy- absorbing metamaterials based on the DNA chain structure are presented. Computer simulation was carried out for preliminary determination of the metamaterial properties. Samples manufactured from Ti6Al4V alloy by the selective laser melting method were tested under quasi-static and dynamic compression. It was established that the specific energy absorption of the metamaterials under dynamic testing was 32.34 J/g, and under quasi-static testing, 14.22 J/g. The metamaterial withstands deformations exceeding 50 % without failure. The obtained results confirm the promising potential of the developed geometry for producing mechanical metamaterials with enhanced energy-absorbing characteristics.

papers.title: Accelerating Fuzzy Formal Concept Analysis via Thermometer-Coded Bit-Slice Transformations and Parallel Search
papers.abstract: Exhaustive concept enumeration in Fuzzy Formal Concept Analysis (FFCA) suffers from severe scalability bottlenecks due to repetitive, pointwise scalar evaluations over the unit interval during search space traversal. To address this, we introduce a structural shift from traditional scalar operations to a tensor-domain algebraic formulation. We reformulate the foundational residuated lattice structure ⟨L, ∧, ∨, ⊗, →, 0, 1⟩ by mapping the monoidal minimum t-norm ⊗ and its residuated implication → into a coordinate-free multi-layer Boolean lattice embedding across an orthogonal rank space, formally proving that all residuated lattice axioms remain structurally invariant under this higher-dimensional embedding. Specifically, the work introduces an algebraic embedding ϕ that maps finite-chain minimum-based residuated lattices into a coordinate-free multi-layer Boolean lattice structure, formally proving that the fundamental residuated lattice axioms remain structurally invariant under this higher-dimensional tensor mapping, enabling fuzzy derivation and closure operations to reduce completely to progressive implication cascades and word-level bitwise conjunctions. Building upon this theoretical foundation, we present Minimum Thermometer-Coded Enumeration (MTCE), a framework that encodes finite-chain minimum-based fuzzy formal concepts into nested thermometer layers while strictly preserving the original object-attribute dimensions without context expansion. Under this representation, fuzzy derivation, closure, and dual rank-domain canonicity checks reduce entirely to layer-wise Boolean conjunctions and progressive implication cascades via word-level bitwise operations. To demonstrate the practical viability of this algebraic formulation, we develop P^MTCE, a multi-threaded, bit-parallel concurrent implementation. Empirical evaluation across benchmark datasets demonstrates order-of-magnitude acceleration over sequential minimum-based CbO baselines (e.g., reducing Iris processing time from 99.1s to 1.0s). These results confirm that the proposed tensor-domain formulation establishes both a rigorous theoretical bridge and a highly efficient computational foundation for finite-chain fuzzy formal concept mining on modern multi-core architectures.

papers.title: Two-Stage Day-Ahead and Intraday Active-Power Regulation of a Flexible Distribution Network Node: Scenario-Based Stochastic Optimization and Model Predictive Control
papers.abstract: Distribution network operators increasingly require demand-side nodes to follow time-varying active-power instructions so that congestion and voltage problems can be mitigated locally. Industrial and commercial users are challenging participants in such schemes: they host substantial controllable electric equipment, yet their internal energy conversion processes must never be interrupted. This paper treats such a user as a flexible node of the distribution network, with the active power exchanged at the point of common coupling as the sole control interface, and proposes a two-stage day-ahead/intraday regulation framework, intended as a transferable scheduling model that parks with comparable resource portfolios can reuse by substituting their own load, renewable, device and price data. On the grid side, the user presents a portfolio of controllable electric resources: a gas-fired combined heat and power (CHP) unit acting as dispatchable local generation, electricity-driven power-to-heat and power-to-cooling units acting as adjustable electric loads, and storage that decouples the timing of the electric adjustment from the rigid internal demand, while the heat and cold balances are handled exclusively as hard internal constraints. The day-ahead layer is a scenario-based stochastic program built from Monte Carlo-sampled, K-means-reduced PV and wind scenarios; the intraday layer is a model predictive controller with a 15 min control interval and a 3 h receding window that corrects the deviation between the day-ahead expected renewable trajectory and the realized renewable output, together with device execution deviations modeled as zero-mean Gaussian perturbations. On a winter day benchmark, activating the full electric portfolio reduces the average node tracking error from 253.5 kW to the numerical zero level and raises the attainment rate from 13.5% to 100%, with the internal heat and cold balances holding as hard constraints on the set-point basis; on the realized basis, where the device execution disturbances are applied, the mean error stays between 12.4 and 13.6 kW and the heat imbalance is zero under the nominal disturbance, the strongest adversarial disturbance examined leaving 8.9 kW in three of the 96 intervals, i.e., 4.2 kWh or 0.05% of the daily heat demand. Under a time-of-use tariff with a 3:1 peak-to-valley ratio, the same portfolio produces a valley-heating, peak-generating schedule that cuts the daily grid purchase from 5.61 MWh to 0.33 MWh, and coordinating the battery on top lowers the daily operating cost by a further 4.7%.

papers.title: Hirota Bilinear Analysis and Physics-Informed Neural Network Simulation for a Sixth-Order (2+1)-Dimensional Generalized Calogero–Bogoyavlenskii–Schiff Equation
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a new sixth-order (2+1)-dimensional generalized Calogero–Bogoyavl enskii–Schiff (S2GCBS) equation and provides exact analytical solutions by using Physics-Informed Neural Network simulation (PINNs). By applying an appropriate traveling wave transformation, the governing nonlinear partial differential equation is reduced to an ordinary differential equation. A systematic solution procedure is then employed to derive several classes of exact solutions. As a result, different types of wave structures are obtained, including hyperbolic function solutions (soliton solutions), trigonometric function solutions (periodic wave solutions), and rational solutions. In particular, the obtained results contain bright soliton solutions, dark soliton solutions, singular soliton solutions, and periodic wave solutions expressed in compact analytical forms. These solutions reveal the rich dynamical behavior of the gCBS model and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in constructing exact solutions for nonlinear evolution equations arising in mathematical physics. The physical characteristics of the obtained solutions are illustrated through several graphical representations.

papers.title: Моделирование процесса кластеризации адресов в блокчейне на основе байесовской оптимизации весов эвристик
papers.abstract: В статье рассматривается задача кластеризации адресов в блокчейне – ключевой метод криптовалютной форензики, используемый при расследовании преступлений с цифровыми активами. Предложен подход к комбинированию трех эвристик кластеризации: множественного входа (Multi-Input Heuristic, MIH), адреса сдачи (Change Address Heuristic, CAH) и временных паттернов (Temporal Pattern Heuristic, TPH). Для комбинирования используется взвешенное голосование, а для подбора весовых коэффициентов и порога объединения применяется байесовская оптимизация с гауссовским процессом в качестве суррогатной модели и функцией сбора ожидаемого улучшения (Expected Improvement). Формализована математическая модель кластеризации с использованием AT-графов, A-графов и E-графов, описаны этапы перехода от графа транзакций к графу сущностей. Проведены три эксперимента на реальных данных из датасета maltemoeser. В первом эксперименте (500 транзакций, 1562 адреса) комбинирование эвристик позволило достичь значения F1-меры (гармоническое среднее между точностью и полнотой) 0,9284, что соответствует уровню наилучшей отдельной эвристики (CAH: 0,9284). Во втором эксперименте (775 транзакций, 2850 адресов) получен F1 = 0,8251, что превышает показатели отдельных эвристик (MIH: 0,8151, CAH: 0,8184, TPH: 0,0838). В третьем эксперименте (990 транзакций, 3445 адресов) получен F1 = 0,8146, что также превышает показатели отдельных эвристик. Результаты экспериментов свидетельствуют в пользу наличия синергетического эффекта предлагаемого подхода. Комбинирование в ряде случаев позволяет частично компенсировать недостатки отдельных эвристик и достичь более высокого качества кластеризации. Изменение структуры данных при увеличении объема выборки приводит к перераспределению весов эвристик, что отражает адаптивность предлагаемого метода. Обоснована практическая применимость метода в реальных расследованиях: эталонная разметка требуется только на этапе калибровки, после чего веса фиксируются для применения на новых данных. Проведен сравнительный анализ с альтернативными подходами машинного обучения. This article examines the problem of blockchain address clustering, a key method in cryptocurrency forensics used in investigating digital asset crimes. An approach combining three clustering heuristics is proposed: Multi-Input Heuristic (MIH), Change Address Heuristic (CAH), and Temporal Pattern Heuristic (TPH). Weighted voting is used for the combination, and Bayesian optimization with a Gaussian process as a surrogate model and an Expected Improvement function is applied to select the weights and the merging threshold. A mathematical clustering model is formalized using AT-graphs, A-graphs, and E-graphs, and the stages of transition from a transaction graph to an entity graph are described. Three experiments are conducted on real data from the maltemoeser dataset. In the first experiment (500 transactions, 1562 addresses), combining the heuristics allowed us to achieve an F1-measure (harmonic mean between precision and recall) of 0.9284, which corresponds to the level of the best individual heuristic (CAH: 0.9284). In the second experiment (775 transactions, 2850 addresses), F1 = 0.8251 was obtained, which exceeds the performance of individual heuristics (MIH: 0.8151, CAH: 0.8184, TPH: 0.0838). In the third experiment (990 transactions, 3445 addresses), F1 = 0.8146 was obtained, which also exceeds the performance of individual heuristics. The experimental results support the presence of a synergistic effect of the proposed approach. In some cases, combining the heuristics makes it possible to partially compensate for the shortcomings of individual heuristics and achieve higher clustering quality. Changes in the data structure with an increase in the sample size lead to a redistribution of the heuristic weights, which reflects the adaptability of the proposed method. The method's practical applicability to real-world investigations is substantiated: reference labeling is required only during the calibration stage, after which the weights are fixed for application to new data. A comparative analysis with alternative machine learning approaches is conducted.

papers.title: Towards trustworthy remaining useful life prediction of bearing based on a Bayesian physics-informed neural network
papers.abstract: Abstract The degradation process of bearings is characterized by pronounced nonlinearity and uncertainty, making it difficult to establish explicit dynamic models that accurately describe their degradation behavior. Moreover, most existing methods provide only deterministic remaining useful life (RUL) estimates and lack effective quantification of predictive uncertainty, thereby limiting their reliability in maintenance planning and operational decision-making. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a trustworthy RUL prediction method for bearings based on a Bayesian physics-informed neural network (BPINN). This method effectively integrates the physics-informed architecture with a Bayesian framework, thereby fully leveraging the enhancement effect of physical information on model interpretability. Simultaneously, it utilizes the probabilistic modeling capability of the Bayesian framework to provide uncertainty estimation for RUL prediction. Experimental results indicate that it can provide RUL predictions with associated uncertainty information, which offers additional decision-support information for predictive maintenance.

papers.title: Surrogate-Based Constrained Single-Objective Bayesian Optimization for Joule-Heated Methane Dry Reforming Reactors
papers.abstract: Joule heating coupled with porous media offers rapid in situ heat generation and a more uniform temperature distribution for DRM reactions, whereas the strong coupling of structural and operating parameters renders conventional trial-and-error optimization inefficient and costly. To tackle this challenge, a multi-physics numerical model for a centrally resistively heated DRM reactor is constructed by coupling Joule heating, flow and heat transfer, multicomponent species transport, and apparent reaction kinetics. A fully connected feedforward neural network (FC-FNN) surrogate model is further established to enable rapid prediction of reactor performance. Seven critical input variables are selected, including reaction temperature, gas hourly space velocity (GHSV), etc., and 9216 simulation samples are generated via numerical simulations for surrogate model training and parametric analysis. The results demonstrate that the Bayesian-optimized FC-FNN model exhibits high predictive accuracy for the core reactor performance metrics, achieving coefficients of determination (R2) above 0.960 for CH4 conversion, CO2 conversion, energy efficiency, and the H2/CO molar ratio. Subsequently, an unknown-constrained alternating Bayesian optimization (UCA-BO) algorithm is adopted to maximize the average reactant conversion under the constraints of H2/CO molar ratio ≥ 0.9 and bed-temperature non-uniformity ≤ 5%. Under the optimized operating conditions, the average reactant conversion reaches 94.12%, accompanied by a H2/CO molar ratio of 0.98, a bed-temperature non-uniformity of 4.53%, and a system energy efficiency of 74.83%. Posterior verification with the trained surrogate model gives slightly lower values (91.28%, 0.91, 4.86%, and 72.36%), all of which remain within the imposed constraints, confirming feasibility. Overall, the proposed integrated framework of numerical simulation, surrogate modeling, and Bayesian optimization enables efficient parameter screening and comprehensive performance optimization of resistively heated porous-media DRM systems, providing a methodological basis for the structural design and operating-parameter optimization of related reactor systems.

papers.title: Reimagining adolescent education with ephegogy: generative AI and active learning in practice
papers.abstract: Purpose This paper introduces ephegogy, a theory addressing the gap between traditional educational models and adolescents' developmental needs in artificial intelligence (AI)-augmented societies. Blending constructivism, connectivism and generativism, it explores how integrating generative AI (GenAI) and active learning can scaffold motivation, autonomy, and relevance for adolescent learners. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods case study conducted in a single secondary-school geography course during 2024–2025. Quantitative data came from matched pre- and post-intervention surveys measuring motivation and self-efficacy (N = 17; N = 11 for the self-efficacy composite) and locus of control (N = 12), using instruments adapted for an under-14, predominantly English-as-an-additional-language cohort. A separate matched engagement survey (N = 24) and an end-of-course co-creation survey (N = 33) provided further data. Qualitative data comprised 74 individual student reflections analysed thematically using the cultural-historical activity theory (CHAT) framework, alongside open-text survey responses from 74 students. The study was designed using three frameworks (self-determination theory, ephegogy and CHAT). Findings Findings are associational and exploratory, specific to this pilot. Composite motivation increased significantly (p = 0.043, d = 0.53), led by a significant rise in school enjoyment (p = 0.028). On a separate instrument, confidence in using AI tools showed the largest single increase (p = 0.016) and motivation relative to traditional courses also rose (p = 0.040); as several items were examined, these are treated as exploratory. Self-efficacy and locus of control showed no reliable change. Qualitatively, choice, the learning contract, and resource autonomy were dominant themes; most students disclosed and reflected on their AI use, and the modal student experience was ambivalent, valuing autonomy while finding it demanding. Research limitations/implications As a single pilot case study with small, matched samples, no control group and a single teacher-researcher as sole coder, findings are context-specific and cannot support causal claims. Future research should evaluate the framework with larger samples, control conditions, and across diverse cultural contexts and disciplines. Practical implications Ephegogy provides actionable strategies for scaffolding student autonomy and ethical AI use within project-based learning. Tools such as the Student-Author Voice (SAV) rubric support metacognitive reflection and responsible co-creation, assessing authored voice rather than relying on AI detection. Social implications Ephegogy provides actionable strategies for scaffolding student autonomy and ethical AI use within project-based learning. Tools such as the SAV rubric support metacognitive reflection and responsible co-creation, assessing authored voice rather than relying on AI detection. Originality/value Ephegogy reconceptualises adolescent education for the AI era as a distinct developmental stage requiring its own framework, operationalised through gradual immersion and the assessment of authored voice. This paper reports an initial classroom pilot offering preliminary, transferable insights rather than confirmatory evidence.

papers.title: Bridge Stability Prediction Using Bayesian-Optimized ConvLSTM
papers.abstract: Abstract Bridge structures are affected by wind loads, traffic loads, and long-term environmental changes. Therefore, stability prediction is crucial for achieving effective bridge health monitoring. This study proposes a convolutional long short-term memory network model based on Bayesian optimization improvement. This model can capture spatiotemporal features in monitoring data. The study collects vibration and wind speed data from cable-stayed bridges. Then, the study uses denoising, interpolation, and normalization techniques for preprocessing. To further optimize feature extraction, the model introduces a grouping space spectrum pyramid pooling structure. Meanwhile, to achieve adaptive tuning of hyperparameters, Bayesian optimization algorithm is adopted. Both experimental and ablation studies show that the proposed model outperforms traditional methods in terms of prediction accuracy and generalization ability. The combination of grouping space spectrum pyramid pooling and Bayesian optimization significantly advances the model's ability to learn spatiotemporal features. This helps to obtain more robust and reliable prediction results. This model can serve as a practical tool for real-time evaluation of bridge stability. Then, the model can provide support for intelligent decision-making in long-term structural health monitoring.

papers.title: Environmental Mechanochemistry: From Force-Induced Reactivity to Aqueous Reaction Platforms
papers.abstract: Abstract Mechanochemistry is increasingly used in environmental research, but is still commonly treated as a material synthesis or pretreatment step rather than a mode of driving reactions that directly affects pathways relevant to pollution control and resource recovery. This Perspective argues that its environmental significance is most evident when force not only changes material properties before use, but also alters how reactions proceed during operation. We compare how force becomes chemically effective in inorganic and organic systems and classify environmental applications according to its primary role. Using zerovalent iron (ZVI) as a representative example, we show that mechanochemistry can simultaneously alleviate multiple bottlenecks in ZVI preparation, storage, and application. Earlier studies have shown that force can regulate ZVI lattice structure, surface state, and interfacial charge transfer. The wet-milling mechanochemical reactor (MCR) extends these effects into aqueous operation by applying force during rather than before reaction. This intensifies solid–liquid contact, accelerates heterogeneous kinetics, and, in some systems, shifts target transformation from surface-confined pathways toward subsurface redistribution and lattice-associated capture. Future advances should identify systems in which force can strengthen reactions sufficiently to open pathways that conventional treatment processes do not readily access.

papers.title: Application of Fourth-Order Cybernetics in Digital Twin-Enabled Adaptive Systems of Systems Operating in High-Stakes Environments
papers.abstract: Modern systems of systems (SoS) operating in high-stakes environments like Distributed Operational System (DOS) are characterized by tightly coupled interactions among human operators, autonomous agents, and heterogeneous technological subsystems. Conventional reliability engineering approaches, which primarily focus on component level failure probabilities and static models are often insufficient for capturing emergent behaviors and nonlinear failure propagation across interconnected sociotechnical systems. This study proposes a cybernetically informed framework that integrates digital twin technology, the Viable System Model (VSM) and an extended Failure Modes and Effects Criticality Analysis (FMECA) methodology to reconceptualise reliability as a dynamic and emergent system property. Digital twins function as continuously updated virtual representations that synchronise real time data, simulation models, and predictive analytics, enabling recursive observation and anticipatory regulation. Their integration with FMECA supports scenario based reliability analysis, allowing the modelling of cascading failures, coordination disruptions and adaptive system responses. The findings demonstrate that reliability emerges from system interactions rather than isolated components, advancing the design of adaptive, resilient, and self-regulating systems operating in complex and uncertain environments. Although applicable to systems of systems related contexts, the framework is intentionally generalised to support broader applications across critical infrastructure, healthcare coordination systems, industrial automation, autonomous transportation, emergency response networks and distributed cyber physical systems. Simulation experiments across distributed systems of systems networks demonstrate how local disturbances propagate through interconnected nodes and are mitigated through cybernetic feedback mechanisms. Simulation experiments across distributed systems of systems networks and demonstrate how local disturbances propagate through interconnected nodes and are mitigated through cybernetic feedback mechanisms. Monte Carlo analysis (n = 1000) indicates high robustness, with operational effectiveness (ζ = 0.929 ± 0.021) and system availability (A = 0.98 ± 0.015). papers.title: Solar-Irradiance Forecasting in Arid Climates: Benchmarking Machine-Learning Models and Probabilistic-Uncertainty Quantification Using Four Years of Riyadh Data
papers.abstract: Precise short-horizon solar-irradiance forecasting is essential for grid-tied inverter control and battery scheduling in arid climates, yet model performance in regions with frequent dust remains under-characterized. This study benchmarks six machine-learning models—Linear Regression, Support Vector Regression (SVR), Random Forest, XGBoost, Gradient Boosting, and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)—for 1-, 3-, and 6-h-ahead Global Horizontal Irradiance forecasting using 34,871 hourly records from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia (2013–2016). All models were tuned with temporal cross-validation and evaluated on an independent 2016 test set. Two feature tracks were evaluated: a full twenty-five-feature set and a three-feature set (hour_sin, hour_cos, GHI_lag_1) selected by recursive feature elimination with 100% bootstrap stability. A four-feature SVR adding doy_cos is the empirical optimum at 1- and 3-h horizons, achieving an RMSE of 65.43 and 77.16 W/m2 (R2 0.956 and 0.948, skill scores 61.5% and 82.8%). At 6 h, Gradient Boosting with the full 25-feature set is best (RMSE 78.99 W/m2). The three-feature LSTM achieves 98.25, 148.84, and 233.47 W/m2. Split-conformal prediction achieves nominal 90% coverage (89.56%, 90.30%, 89.65%) with CRPS of 25.94, 31.36, and 32.42 W/m2, and intervals 7–21% narrower than quantile regression. A matched-condition dust analysis shows no statistically significant difference between dusty and clean days at 1- and 3-h horizons, while at 6 h, dusty days are significantly easier to forecast (37% lower RMSE, 95% CI [−37.46, −11.04]). A reserve allocation simulation using the four-feature SVR shows 9.1% savings at 1 h, 3.6% at 3 h, and 2.4% at 6 h at 94.9% empirical coverage. Rolling-origin validation across two temporal windows confirms stability (SVR standard deviation ≤ 1.8 W/m2).

papers.title: Twenty-First Century Skills in Psychology Education: A Curriculum Inquiry of Master's Programs
papers.abstract: In contemporary work environments, psychology graduates are expected to demonstrate 21st-century skills, including collaboration, communication, and critical thinking. Recognizing these demands, this study aimed to investigate to what extent and how psychology master's programs in the Netherlands integrate 21st-century skills into curricula. First, we conducted a document analysis of the intended learning outcomes (ILOs) of all psychology master's programs ( N = 28) at Dutch research universities. Qualitative content analysis of the ILOs revealed that the 21st-century skills critical thinking, communication, initiative and self-management, and productivity were addressed in all programs’ ILOs. Next, to extend the document analysis, we conducted a case study of an organizational psychology master's program to examine how skills-related ILOs were realized in curriculum components. Results showed that the curriculum provided extensive opportunities to develop 21st-century skills through active learning practices such as group discussions, case assignments, role-plays, and simulations. We also found notable discrepancies between the ILOs and the skills emphasized in learning goals, instructional materials, and assessments, indicating that a broader scope of skills was being taught than was formally articulated. The findings contribute to the literature and educational practices by providing insights into the integration of 21st-century skills in master's programs and informing future curriculum developments.

papers.title: Chebyshev–Legendre Collocation for HEV Energy Management: Regularity, Convergence, and Benchmarks
papers.abstract: This paper presents a Chebyshev–Legendre (CL) collocation method for the optimal energy management of hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs). The method combines spectral collocation with a regularity analysis. We prove that the collocation error decays algebraically with an asymptotic rate of p=3/2 when at least one kink-type switching time is present. We also prove spectral convergence when no active control constraint is present. We first verify the method using a scalar linear-quadratic regulator (LQR) benchmark. We then apply it to a constrained HEV optimal control problem. The model includes a discontinuous fuel map, but the considered drive cycles do not activate this discontinuity. The optimal solution exhibits bang-bang behavior at the battery power bounds. We compare the CL solution with a basic equivalent consumption minimization strategy (ECMS), an adaptive ECMS (A-ECMS), and a model predictive control strategy (MPC-CL). We also compare the CL method directly with standard Chebyshev and Legendre pseudospectral methods. The results show that the CL method achieves the same accuracy as the Legendre method with reduced computational overhead. Furthermore, we validate the method’s robustness using a new low-load driving cycle that activates the fuel-map jump discontinuity. The offline CL solution and basic ECMS yield statistically indistinguishable costs, with a difference of approximately 0.01%. Basic ECMS is not a real-time strategy. Therefore, we classify it as an offline benchmark alongside CL. Among the evaluated real-time strategies, A-ECMS with Kp=1 achieves the lowest cost increase (+2.53%). MPC-CL follows with a cost increase of +7.47%. More aggressive A-ECMS gains (Kp≥5) produce cost increases between 11.7% and 13.0%. We estimate the numerical self-convergence rate of the control using a least-squares fit. The resulting rate is pL2fit=1.466. This rate agrees with the theoretical prediction p=3/2 to within 2.3%. Finally, we numerically verify each item of the structural assumption on the offline solution.

papers.title: Accurate State-of-Charge Estimation of Lithium-Ion Batteries Using Bayesian- and PSO-Optimized NARX Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Abstract Accurate state-of-charge (SoC) estimation is essential for reliable energy management in electric vehicles, particularly under varying operating and temperature conditions. This study develops a recurrent neural-network-based SoC estimator that exploits battery cur rent, terminal voltage, ambient temperature, and delayed output information to capture the temporal dynamics of the battery system. To address the strong dependence of the nonlinear autoregressive network with exogenous inputs (NARX) architecture on its hy perparameters, two optimization strategies are considered, namely Bayesian Optimization (BO) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The resulting BO-NARX and PSO-NARX estimators are evaluated against a conventional Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) under dif ferent driving cycles and temperature conditions. The results show that both optimized NARX models provide accurate SoC tracking and generally outperform the EKF, while their relative performance varies depending on the operating conditions. These ndings highlight the importance of both temporal modeling and hyperparameter optimization for robust SoC estimation in battery management systems.

papers.title: Simulation-Based Basic Life Support Training: A QuasiExperimental Study Comparing Peyton’s Four-Step Approach with Traditional Teaching Among Undergraduate Medical Students
papers.abstract: Background: Basic Life Support (BLS) competence is an essential requirement for medical graduates; however, traditional teaching may provide limited opportunities for active learning and structured practice. Peyton's FourStep Approach (PFSA) is a learner-centred method for teaching procedural skills, but evidence regarding its effectiveness in BLS skill acquisition and retention among undergraduate medical students in India remains limited. Objectives: To evaluate the effectiveness of Peyton's Four-Step Approach compared with Traditional Teaching Method (TTM) in improving immediate BLS skill performance and one-month skill retention among undergraduate medical students. Secondary objectives were to assess learner satisfaction and confidence with the two teaching methods. Methods: A quasi-experimental study was conducted among 100 third-year undergraduate medical students at GSL Medical College, Rajahmundry, Andhra Pradesh. Participants were non-randomly allocated into an experimental group receiving BLS training using Peyton's Four-Step Approach (n = 50) and a control group receiving Traditional Teaching Method (n = 50). BLS skills were assessed using a 15-item Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE) checklist before training, immediately after training, and one month after the intervention. Student satisfaction and confidence were also assessed. Data were analysed using independent samples t-test and Chi-square test, with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant. Results: Baseline OSCE scores were comparable between the PFSA and TTM groups (5.82 ± 1.34 vs. 5.68 ± 1.41; p = 0.612). The PFSA group demonstrated significantly higher immediate post-training OSCE scores than the TTM group (12.46 ± 1.18 vs. 10.84 ± 1.47; mean difference: 1.62; p < 0.001). At one-month follow-up, skill retention remained significantly higher in the PFSA group (11.72 ± 1.29 vs. 9.63 ± 1.58; mean difference: 2.09; p < 0.001). Student satisfaction was higher in the PFSA group than in the TTM group (90% vs. 16%; χ² = 54.96; p < 0.001). Similarly, a greater proportion of students in the PFSA group reported confidence in performing BLS skills (88% vs. 10%; χ² = 30.43; p < 0.001). Conclusions: Peyton's Four-Step Approach was more effective than Traditional Teaching Method for improving immediate BLS skill performance and one-month skill retention among undergraduate medical students. The approach was also associated with greater student satisfaction and confidence. Incorporating structured, learnercentred approaches such as PFSA into undergraduate BLS training may enhance the acquisition and retention of essential resuscitation skills.

papers.title: An intelligent computational modeling framework for robotic kinematics and control using neural networks with genetic optimization and reinforcement learning
papers.abstract: This paper presents an intelligent computational modeling framework that integrates data-driven surrogate modeling methods into the simulation and control pipeline of a six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) industrial manipulator. Traditional model-based approaches for robotic kinematics, dynamics, and trajectory optimization face inherent limitations when confronted with high-dimensional nonlinearities, kinematic singularities, and real-time computational constraints. To address these challenges, we propose a unified architecture in which Genetic Algorithms (GA), Neural Networks (NN), and Reinforcement Learning (RL) are systematically repositioned as surrogate solvers within a coherent computational modeling workflow. The core technical novelty lies not in the individual algorithms—which are well established—but in the unified agent computing layer that couples them through formally defined interfaces, enabling end-to-end surrogate-based simulation-to-control deployment. The framework encompasses: (1) a GA-based trajectory optimizer with formal time complexity analysis O(N·P·G) and empirical convergence validation, benchmarked against sequential quadratic programming (SQP) under identical constraints; (2) a feedforward neural network serving as a surrogate inverse kinematics solver, accompanied by generalization error bounds and the scaling of prediction accuracy with training data, compared against damped least-squares (DLS) and Levenberg–Marquardt (LM) numerical solvers; (3) an RL-based adaptive control policy trained via DDPG and benchmarked against PPO and SAC, and further compared against model predictive control (MPC), model-reference adaptive control (MRAC), and sliding-mode control (SMC) under identical disturbance conditions. Comprehensive numerical analyses include computational complexity, convergence curves, FLOP counts, and inference latency. A co-simulation validation protocol quantifies numerical synchronization error between virtual and physical platforms. A quantitative integration ablation study demonstrates that the coupled GA–NN–RL pipeline outperforms any single-module or two-module configuration, and an extended robustness characterization reveals the RL controller’s degradation boundary beyond 2.5 Nm disturbance torque. Experimental results demonstrate that the NN surrogate achieves a 4.2× speedup over analytical IK with mean joint error 0.41°, the GA optimizer reduces cycle time by 28.8%, and the RL agent achieves adaptive path correction within 0.3 s under ± 2 mm perturbations. The contributions are fourfold: (i) a unified framework integrating GA, NN, RL through a dedicated agent computing layer; (ii) rigorous numerical analyses with controlled comparisons against established baselines; (iii) a validated co-simulation protocol; (iv) a quantitative integration ablation and extended robustness analysis.

papers.title: A Human–Vehicle Cooperative Path Following Control Method for Intelligent Vehicles
papers.abstract: To address smoothness and safety issues in driving authority switching for human–machine co-driving intelligent vehicles, a hierarchical control strategy is proposed. The upper-layer controller utilizes a two-point preview model for human driving and a radial basis function neural network-based nonsingular fast terminal sliding mode controller with a heuristic gain adaptive tuning mechanism (RBFNN-HGATM-NFTSMC) for autonomous tracking. The lower-layer authority switching controller employs a driving risk-based finite state machine, integrating a risk-switching strategy and a cost function-based authority return mechanism. CarSim/Simulink co-simulations show that, compared to model predictive control, the upper-layer controller reduces maximum lateral errors by 77.7% and 66.2% under medium- and high-speed conditions, respectively. Compared with standard RBFNN-NFTSMC, it reduces lateral and heading errors by 56.2% and 11.9% at high speeds. With the decision logic held fixed, the risk-mapped transition lowers the takeover jerk peak by 35.75% and the return-phase jerk by 91.4% relative to an instantaneous transfer, at the cost of a larger transient lateral error during the handover. Under high-speed sudden distraction, the maximum lateral tracking error is 1.17 m. Under extreme parameter mismatch conditions, lateral and heading errors are reduced by 88.5% and 87.1% compared to standard NFTSMC, indicating robustness of the proposed controller under the tested parameter mismatch.

papers.title: Hybridization of the weighted distance method with directional bat algorithm for NMPC tuning
papers.abstract: This work presents a hybrid optimization algorithm that combines the Weighted Distance Method and the Directional Bat Algorithm to improve the efficiency and robustness of solving nonlinear model predictive control problems. The proposed hybrid framework integrates the global exploration capability of the Directional Bat Algorithm with the local exploitation and adaptive refinement properties of the Weighted Distance Method. In the first stage, the Directional Bat Algorithm generates a diverse set of candidate solutions by using adaptive mechanisms for frequency, amplitude, and random movement, thereby ensuring broad coverage of the search space and preventing premature convergence to local minima. Subsequently, the Weighted Distance Method refines these solutions by computing weighted directional vectors, which are updated at each iteration based on the population mean distance and each agent’s proximity to the global best individual. The sequential combination of both strategies achieves an effective balance between exploration and exploitation, resulting in greater stability, improved convergence performance, and higher-quality optimal solutions. On a standard suite of thirty benchmark functions in dimensions 10, 30, and 50, the hybrid ranks third among five optimizers: it outperforms both of its constituent algorithms but does not surpass the Differential Evolution and Particle Swarm baselines, confirming that the sequential coupling yields a stronger optimizer than either component alone. On the tuning of a nonlinear model predictive controller for a Van de Vusse reactor, the proposed hybrid scheme achieves competitive closed-loop tracking performance compared with the standalone methods while improving convergence stability and robustness to initialization, highlighting its potential for complex nonlinear control applications.

papers.title: Intelligent detection of grouting fullness defects and 3D porosity quantification in prefabricated building sleeves via multiscale Swin feature fusion and approximate uncertainty quantification
papers.abstract: Grouted splice sleeve connections are critical to precast-concrete construction, yet concealed under-grouting defects are difficult to assess from external inspection. This study presents Swin-MFF-BUQ, a dual-pathway framework for uncertainty-aware sleeve assessment. The 2D pathway processes impact-echo and ultrasonic-array time–frequency maps and predicts an analysis-domain anomaly-support mask together with a five-class fullness grade; the mask represents signal-domain anomaly support rather than a physical-space void map. The separately parameterized 3D pathway processes industrial computed-tomography (CT) volumes and estimates physical void geometry and porosity descriptors. Both pathways use deformable-window Swin encoders, bidirectional cross-scale weighted fusion, and uncertainty-aware heads. Experiments used 240 sleeve specimens at five fullness levels, yielding 12,000 records per sensing modality, and a 36-volume CT development collection. On a specimen-held-out signal test split, the 2D pathway achieved 91.4±0.3% mIoU and 95.1±0.2% image-wise Dice, a 2.8-point mIoU improvement over the strongest of eight 2D-compatible baselines. Fullness grading reached 96.8±0.4% accuracy and 96.5% macro-F1. On held-out volumes within the CT development collection, porosity regression yielded an MAE of 0.62±0.05 percentage points, an RMSE of 0.84 percentage points, and R2=0.976. Temperature scaling reduced ECE from 0.034 to 0.021; uncertainty correlated with segmentation error (Spearman ρ=0.81), and deferring the 10% most uncertain cases increased retained-set mIoU to 93.6%. Standard 2D inference required 38 ms per 512×512 map. The findings support uncertainty-aware signal screening and CT-based volumetric characterization; independent sleeve-level validation remains necessary for the developmental CT results.
