papers.title: Advances in injectable liposome–microspheres platforms for osteoarthritis therapy: from sustained delivery to multifunctional disease modification
papers.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic, whole-joint disorder marked by progressive cartilage degradation, subchondral bone remodeling, synovial inflammation, and capsular fibrosis, affecting over 500 million individuals worldwide. Current pharmacotherapies are mainly palliative, with no approved disease-modifying osteoarthritis drugs (DMOADs). Intra-articular (IA) injection provides direct joint access but is hampered by rapid drug clearance and short residence times. Injectable liposome–microsphere (iLMP) systems have recently emerged as integrative delivery platforms that synergistically combine the high loading capacity, targeting versatility, and stimuli-responsiveness of liposomes with the sustained release, lubrication, mechanical support, and protective shielding of hydrogel microspheres. This “nano-in-micro” hierarchical architecture enables prolonged joint retention, spatiotemporally controlled drug release, active cell/tissue targeting, and even gene editing, thereby shifting OA management from symptom alleviation toward true disease modification. In this review, we systematically examine the rational design of iLMPs, covering liposomal composition and functionalization, microsphere fabrication technologies (microfluidics, electrospraying, 3D bioprinting, emulsification), and assembly strategies (embedding, anchoring, adsorption, and matrix hybridization). We then detail their physicochemical determinants—size, surface charge, rheology, and degradation kinetics—and discuss the multifaceted therapeutic mechanisms, including sustained pharmacokinetic modulation, boundary lubrication, active/passive targeting, enzyme/ROS/pH-responsive release, nucleic acid delivery, and exosome-hybrid biofunctionalization. Finally, we critically analyze current translational barriers (scale-up, long-term stability, safety, and cost) and outline future directions toward intelligent, personalized, and combination regimens. With continued advances in biomaterials, microengineering, and precision medicine, iLMPs are poised to become a cornerstone of next-generation OA therapy.

papers.title: Impact of family dynamics on the eating behaviors of overweight or obese children: A qualitative study of parents or grandparents
papers.abstract: Background Obesity has become a major global public health issue. The occurrence and progression of childhood overweight and obesity result from the combined effects of multiple factors, including genetic factors, lifestyle, psychological factors, and the social environment. Among these, the family, as the primary setting where children acquire early life experiences and develop initial behavioral habits, exerts a profound influence on the development and reinforcement of their eating behaviors. However, previous studies have rarely considered the family as a dynamic interactive system when examining its role in shaping children's eating behaviors. In particular, in-depth qualitative exploration remains lacking regarding how specific processes, such as role division and intergenerational interactions among family members, influence children's eating behaviors. Objective To explore how family dynamics influence the eating behaviors of children with overweight/obesity from the perspectives of parents or grandparents. Methods A qualitative study was conducted using purposive sampling to recruit 19 parents/grandparents of children with overweight or obesity for semi-structured in-depth interviews. Van Manen's data analysis method was applied for thematic extraction and interpretive analysis. Results Three themes and ten subthemes were identified. Theme 1 focused on interaction patterns within the nuclear family in child dietary management, including four subthemes: The theme 1 was relevant with the impact of parental weight-loss attitude differences on collaborative dietary management, the maternalization of feeding responsibilities and the time-energy pressure on mothers, the shaping of children's eating behaviors through parent–child interaction styles, and excessive food provision driven by concerns about nutritional deficiency. Theme 2 addressed the multiple effects of intergenerational involvement on children's eating behaviors, encompassing three subthemes: practice patterns and intergenerational division of labor in grandparental participation in child dietary management, intergenerational differences in dietary management beliefs against the backdrop of social change, and the intergenerational transmission and continuity of family dietary habits. Theme 3 pertained to the empowerment of family dietary management by external support systems, comprising three subthemes: reconstruction of family feeding patterns triggered by medical diagnosis, the sustaining role of social media platforms in promoting healthy eating behaviors, and the implementation of health tools to assist eating behavior monitoring. Conclusion The formation and modification of eating behaviors in children with overweight and obesity are jointly shaped by interactions within the nuclear family, intergenerational involvement, and external support systems. Discrepancies in parental weight-loss attitudes weaken feeding coordination; the maternalization of feeding responsibilities places mothers under dual time and energy pressures between career and family; authoritarian parent–child interactions tend to trigger child resistance and avoidance behaviors; and concerns about growth and development may drive parents toward excessive food provision. At the intergenerational level, grandparents demonstrate both autonomy and adaptability in child dietary management, with their traditional beliefs being updateable through external information input and active learning; nevertheless, family dietary habits tend to persist through intergenerational shared meals, forming entrenched taste preferences and eating routines in children. Medical diagnosis serves as a critical turning point, while social media platforms and online health-related applications empower family dietary management through informational, emotional, and instrumental support respectively. Future childhood obesity interventions are recommended to shift from individual behavior guidance toward to combination with family-system support, assisting family members in reaching consensus on dietary management rules and integrating external resources such as medical services, social media platforms, and health tools to construct a family-centered weight management support system for children.

papers.title: A Critical Theoretical Review of Moreno’s Psychodrama and Its Dimensions in Educational Practice
papers.abstract: The use of new knowledge, as expressed in psychodrama, helps to understand individuality through the study of the group, while at the same time allowing and encouraging improvement and change in the individual for own and others’ benefit. Psychodrama is an alternative method of psychotherapy developed by the Romanian psychiatrist Jacob Moreno (1889–1974). Moreno offered one of the most influential theories (Role Theory) in psychology and psychiatry, explaining the impact of social roles on an individual’s behavior. This paper determines the effect of psychodrama as an experiential method that enhances emotional awareness and communication skills of adolescents. It discusses criticisms regarding the scientific validity and practical suitability of psychodramatic techniques in educational settings, such as role-playing, role reversal, doubling, and other experiential methods that promote active learning, empathy, and problem-solving, and the methods through which key techniques involve sharing and reflection, highlighting the fundamental principles of role-based learning. Although psychodrama throughout the ages has been criticized for its reliance on subjective experience and challenges of systematic evaluation, research is required to emphasize the effectiveness of psychodramatic methodologies and techniques in diverse educational contexts, ensuring integration into inclusiveness and contemporary teaching and learning environments.

papers.title: EBSD study of microstructure produced during laser powder bed fusion of 17-4 PH martensitic steel
papers.abstract: Electron backscatter diffraction was applied to investigate the broad aspects of the microstructure produced during laser powder beam fusion of 17-4 PH steel. It was found that the laser powder beam fusion process involved the -ferrite-to-austenite-to-martensite phase transformation sequence. Remarkably, the solidification <100> + <111> fiber texture in -ferrite was essentially inherited by the final martensitic phase, i.e., the texture-memory effect was observed. It was also revealed that the -ferrite-to-austenite transformation involved a strict selection of crystallographic variants. This led to a pronounced crystallographic preference of 60° <111> boundaries in the austenitic phase. The core result of this study was an integral pattern of microstructural changes during laser powder beam fusion from a solidification stage down to ambient conditions.

papers.title: Depth-specific characterization of bone microarchitecture in the femoral head: implications for osteoarthritis and osteoporosis research
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Osteoarthritis (OA) and osteoporosis (OP) are highly prevalent musculoskeletal diseases characterized by cartilage loss and increased subchondral bone formation and by systemic bone mass reduction, respectively. The femoral head is commonly examined in both OA and OP research, yet both conditions may coexist in the same patient, making it unclear how local cartilage degeneration and systemic bone mineral density (BMD), as a marker of OP-related skeletal status, contribute to bone microarchitectural changes at different depths. Methods Femoral heads were obtained from 30 patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty for hip OA. Ex vivo high-resolution peripheral quantitative computed tomography (HR-pQCT) was performed on the entire femoral head, followed by computational segmentation of the subchondral mineralized plate (SMP) and five concentric trabecular regions. Depth-specific bone microarchitectural parameters were analyzed in relation to histologically assessed cartilage degeneration and systemic BMD measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). Results The cohort had a mean age of 75.4 ± 9.5 years, 53.3% were female, and patients spanned the spectrum of normal BMD (36.7%), osteopenia (46.7%), and osteoporosis (16.7%). Trabecular volumetric tissue mineral density (Tb.vTMD), bone volume to tissue volume (BV/TV), and trabecular thickness (Tb.Th) showed an initial decrease in the superficial trabecular regions, followed by a progressive increase toward deeper regions, whereas cyst-like void volume continuously decreased with depth and almost completely disappeared beyond 9.84 mm in depth. Cartilage degeneration independently predicted subchondral bone microstructure within the SMP and in superficial to intermediate trabecular regions (up to 13.12 mm in depth). Specifically, higher OARSI grades were associated with higher SMP.Th, Tb.vTMD, BV/TV, and Tb.Th. Systemic BMD T-score emerged as an independent predictor of trabecular bone parameters across all depths and represented the sole determinant of BV/TV and Tb.Th in the deepest trabecular region (beyond 13.12 mm depth), while cartilage degeneration was not associated with trabecular bone parameters in the deepest trabecular region. Conclusions Our findings showcase spatially distinct contributions of cartilage degeneration and systemic skeletal status to subchondral bone remodeling, identifying depth as a critical determinant in the analysis of osteochondral alterations in hip OA. Specifically, our findings emphasize that systemic BMD should be considered a covariate in OA research and that deep regions of the femoral head should be used for OP research to minimize potential confounding by local OA-related effects.

papers.title: Predictive Information Loss at Physical Model Interfaces: Sufficient State Transfer and Information-Retention Horizons
papers.abstract: Coupled physical models can preserve conserved quantities and a current observable while discarding upstream information needed for future prediction. We formulate this loss relative to a shared information record, an additional record available to the sending module, and a specified future observation. Conditional mutual information gives the irreducible expected logarithmic-score loss of compression; a separate relative-entropy term measures downstream misspecification. A linear– Gaussian specialization yields a fixed-rank state-retention rule. A positive, energy-balanced threereservoir benchmark preserves total energy and instantaneous luminosity while hiding a coordinate that affects later emission. At the declared noise level, a nominal 95 % plug-in interval achieves 29.09 % ensemble coverage near the early loss maximum. Exact marginalization restores ensemble coverage at 3.50 times the width of the state-informed reference; transmitting the extra coordinate removes this interface loss only when it is already available upstream. A model-specific analytic bound guarantees a marginal information-retention interval of at least 0.02736 time units for a tolerance of 0.05 nats, compared with a numerically located first crossing at 0.02820. Joint-target calculations show why cancellation at one forecast time cannot certify an entire curve. Noise sensitivity and correlated-readout tests delimit the numerical claims. The results concern a controlled interface and do not infer an unknown source state or validate a real astrophysical event. Keywords: predictive sufficiency; model coupling; uncertainty quantification; information loss; adaptivecomputation; time-domain astrophysics.

papers.title: Glycol chitosan thermogels: a versatile platform for advanced drug delivery.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Injectable thermogels are promising localized drug delivery platforms as their temperature-triggered in situ gelation facilitates practical administration. However, conventional systems suffer from high critical gelation concentrations, limited biodegradability, cytotoxicity, or acidic degradation, which can cause local inflammation. Glycol chitosan (GC)-based thermogels have emerged as a promising alternative, combining aqueous solubility at physiological pH, biodegradability, biocompatibility, mucoadhesion, low-concentration gelation, and structural versatility. AREAS COVERED: This review comprehensively examines GC-based thermogels, highlighting how hydrophobic modifications govern their structure-property relationships and thermo-responsive gelation. It evaluates their performance as localized reservoirs for small-molecule drugs, biomacromolecules, and genes across challenging anatomical sites with rapid physiological clearance, including ocular, inner ear, and vaginal sites, while summarizing emerging biofunctional applications in cell delivery, wound healing, and 3D biofabrication. Recent advances in prodrug thermogels, dual crosslinked networks, and biohybrid formulations are also discussed. EXPERT OPINION: To advance GC-based thermogels toward clinical implementation, formulation design must prioritize controlled degradation synchronized with payload release and therapeutic duration. Translation will require standardized polymer characterization, reproducible and scalable manufacturing, sterilization-compatible processing, long-term local safety assessment, and rigorous benchmarking in clinically relevant models. Ultimately, indication-specific formulations with functionality tailored to defined therapeutic needs are more likely to achieve clinical translation than a universal platform approach.

papers.title: OdorSpaces: Visual-Olfactory Embodied Navigation in 3D Environments
papers.abstract: Olfaction provides critical information about airborne chemical cues, yet it remains largely underexplored in embodied AI, with limited prior machine olfaction work focusing primarily on semantic odor perception. We introduce OdorSpaces, a physics-based simulation platform and benchmark for visual-olfactory embodied navigation. OdorSpaces augments Habitat-Sim with 3D odor transport and dispersion simulated by Fire Dynamics Simulator (FDS), enabling agents to navigate photorealistic indoor environments using both visual and olfactory observations. The benchmark includes two representative source-seeking scenarios: invisible gas-leak localization and early-stage fire localization. We develop an initial multimodal reinforcement learning policy that integrates visual observations and olfactory measurements over time. Experiments show that the policy outperforms a diverse set of baselines, establishing a strong reference for future research on visual-olfactory embodied navigation.

papers.title: Translate, then decide: asymptotic optimality of latent-space control in bistable systems
papers.abstract: This paper asks whether an optimal decision can be separated from the physical dynamics on which it acts. It studies this question through minimum-energy barrier crossing in scalar bistable systems. It characterizes the finite-horizon optimal feedback and shows that, as the horizon grows, it converges to a law that doubles and reverses the drift while it opposes crossing, and switches off once the barrier is passed. In physical coordinates, this law inherits the plant's nonlinearity, entangling decision and dynamics. We show that a plant-specific translation of state, input, and time maps every double well in the considered class to the same unit-rate linear world model, allowing a downstream decision stage to use a single plant-independent control primitive. This separation generally loses optimality at finite horizons because the translation does not preserve the physical control energy. Nevertheless, we prove that the excess physical energy of the layered controller vanishes as the horizon grows and that its limiting feedback reproduces the asymptotic optimum exactly. Thus, translation and optimization generally do not commute at a finite horizon, but commute in the asymptotic limit.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Learning of Universal Latent Spaces for Operator Learning
papers.abstract: Neural operators fit their representation of functions to the task they are trained on, so every new task rebuilds a reduced space from labeled data. Following the self-supervised pre-training that made representations shareable in natural language processing and computer vision, we decouple representation learning from operator learning. A functional autoencoder is pre-trained on analytic functions synthesized on the fly, with no solver and no labels, to represent functions on arbitrary point clouds, and the latent space it induces is frozen and reused across tasks. The representation is exactly equivariant to translation, dilation, and amplitude, and reconstructs solutions of partial differential equations (PDEs) and natural images on geometries it never saw. Being task-agnostic, the latent space can be interpreted in its own right. The whole space is used and decodes to valid fields, it preserves the ordering of distances between physical fields, its geodesics interpolate physical evolutions, and edit directions transfer across fields. With frozen representation maps, a dataset is encoded once and a neural operator is trained entirely on cached embeddings, which saves memory and training time. On 28 tasks in fluid dynamics, solid mechanics, acoustics, and the Helmholtz and Poisson equations, this paradigm can exceed the accuracy of state-of-the-art end-to-end architectures, with up to an order of magnitude higher throughput and memory savings that fit models nearly two orders of magnitude larger on consumer-grade GPUs. At inference, latent rollouts run up to an order of magnitude faster than regular rollouts, and chunked inference processes functions of over half a billion points on a single consumer-grade GPU.

papers.title: From Type to Token: Petri Nets, Individual Token Philosophy, and Individualized Causal Effects
papers.abstract: Structural Causal Models and Bayesian Networks are the dominant framework for representing causal relations. They are fundamentally type-level formalisms since their estimands, Average Treatment Effects and Conditional Average Treatment Effects, are properties of distributions over populations, not of individual units. When treatment effects exhibit unbounded heterogeneity, these estimands collapse. What persists is the structural, token-level core of causation.   We argue that Petri Nets under the Individual Token Philosophy are the natural representation of these token-level causal structures. We develop a formal translation from Bayesian Networks to Petri Nets, providing a two-layer account of individualized causality. The PN layer provides a structural representation of causal mechanisms that does not rest on distributional assumptions. In turn, a conformal prediction layer quantifies causal effects with finite-sample coverage guarantees. Together they constitute a complete account of individual causal effects.

papers.title: ARIDA - Active railway infrastructure dataset annotation using neural network predictions
papers.abstract: Modern railway perception requires large comprehensive image datasets, but creating them is slowed by manual labeling, especially for track polylines and other complex infrastructure geometry. This paper presents the Active Railway Infrastructure Dataset Annotation framework, a railway-specific semi-automated pipeline that converts instance predictions from a mask scoring instance segmentation network into bounding-boxes, polygons, polylines, and paired polylines. To keep automatic track geometry annotation reliable without ground truth, it applies confidence thresholds and an unique contour-agreement quality score as an acceptance gate. An active learning loop ranks remaining images by uncertainty and adapts the number of manual queries per cycle. This is achieved through a novel quantity control mechanism, in which easy images are auto-accepted and human effort targets hard cases. Experiments on disjoint, diverse imagery and time-sequential, redundant imagery quantify effort reduction and accuracy trade-offs, achieving about two thirds reduction in the disjoint regime and up to 93% in the sequential regime. The study also provides guidance for initial label budgets and stopping to avoid over-annotation.

papers.title: Contact-Implicit Whole-Body Trajectory Optimization for Dynamic Humanoid Locomotion on Parameterizable Uneven Terrain
papers.abstract: This letter presents a trajectory planner for humanoid robots to perform dynamic motions on complex, parameterizable terrains using a contact-implicit whole-body optimization framework. The planner generates feasible movements without predefined contact sequences, considering the robot's full dynamics and kinematics. To plan bipedal locomotion on steps, ramps, and other terrains, we propose a mathematical model to approximate ground geometry with a smooth surface. The rigid interaction between the robot and the ground is modeled via novel contact constraints, extending the domain of applicability from flat and horizontal surfaces to any arbitrary smooth surface. Effectiveness is demonstrated using nonlinear programming to plan motions on various terrain topologies. We also explore dynamic trajectory generation by embedding high-level requirements in the cost function and the initial guess. Preliminary feasibility tests were conducted over non-coplanar terrains, both in simulation and on the real robot ErgoCub.

papers.title: Generalized Hyperrectangular Prediction Sets in Multivariate Conformal Prediction
papers.abstract: In multivariate conformal prediction, many nonconformity scores yield prediction sets with complex geometry (e.g., ellipsoids or density level sets) that are difficult to interpret and visualize. Hyperrectangles offer a practical alternative by providing one interval per output. We extend this notion to Cartesian products of arbitrary one-dimensional sets, which we call generalized hyperrectangles. We introduce a rectangularization framework that turns any continuous multivariate nonconformity score, or conditional density, into one yielding generalized hyperrectangular prediction sets with finite-sample coverage. We establish key geometric properties of our rectangularization framework and provide useful intuitions on generalized hyperrectangles. We further establish a representation theorem showing that a broad class of hyperrectangular conformal methods based on max-aggregated coordinate-wise scores can be interpreted as rectangularizations of implicit conditional densities. Through synthetic and real-world experiments, we quantify the efficiency cost of rectangularization, while highlighting its benefits, especially for practical applications of uncertainty quantification.

papers.title: Objective-Conditioned Active Preference Learning for Multi-Objective Alignment
papers.abstract: Aligning large language models (LLMs) with several objectives, such as helpfulness, harmlessness, and honesty, typically relies on preference judgment for each objective, growing the annotation cost linearly with the number of objectives. Active preference learning can reduce this cost by selecting the comparisons whose labels are expected to change the policy most. Existing remedies either lack an objective-aware query selection mechanism for the multi-objective setting or regard conflicting preferences as harmful, therefore excluding them from the training data. We introduce OGC-DPO (Objective-conditioned Gradient Coverage DPO), an active learning framework that treats each (response pair, objective) combination as a separate query and measures its informativeness through the policy's own implicit gradient, without relying on an external reward model. OGC-DPO then selects the queries that most expand each objective's gradient coverage. Empirical experiments across varying numbers of objectives demonstrate the effectiveness of OGC-DPO over existing active preference learning methods under the same annotation cost. Further analysis demonstrates that informative conflicts, rather than being uniformly harmful, provide a useful policy training signal.

papers.title: Jev with Foresight: Safe Language-Guided Autonomous Driving via a Language World Model
papers.abstract: Large language models understand passengers' driving commands, but as driving agents they reason in generated text for seconds and must infer each action's consequences implicitly from the scene. We present Jev-AD, which pairs Jev, a typed decision model that answers predefined questions with probabilities, not generated text, with a language world model that predicts for every candidate action how nearby vehicles move over the next two seconds. Code turns these predictions into foreseen consequences, which Jev compares instead of inferring them from coordinates. In simulated highway merging (500 car-episodes), this foresight lowers the same decision model's collision rate from 26.0% to 2.4% at 0.25 seconds per decision, and Jev-AD achieves the passenger's intent in 93% of free-form command trials. In 500 replayed real-world NGSIM episodes, foresight lowers the collision rate from 48.2% to 2.8%, and the world model, learned from this traffic, foresees 93% of dangerous actions. Project page: https://ys-qu.github.io/jev-ad-website.

papers.title: SurgTransfer: Multi-Step Latent Action Modeling for Action Transfer in Surgical World Model
papers.abstract: Surgical world models have the potential to provide intra-operative guidance, accelerate risk-free training and facilitate transfer of expert surgical maneuvers. However, the use of world models for transferring surgical expertise has been largely unexplored. Moreover, recent approaches in this domain have mainly relied on ground truth kinematics actions or expert annotations for specific tasks, limiting their applicability beyond the narrow range of tasks with ground-truth annotations. In contrast, existing works in the natural domain have shown promising results in learning latent actions solely from unlabeled videos and transferring the learned actions across contexts. We observe that this paradigm is short-sighted for the surgical domain, failing to capture the hierarchical and goal-directed structure of surgical procedures. Thus, we propose a novel multi-step action learning framework to learn context-invariant latent actions that are easily transferable across various surgical contexts. We perform extensive experiments on the publicly available datasets, SurgToolLoc-2022 and PitVis-2023, verifying our approach with both quantitative metrics and qualitative evaluation by surgical experts. We have published our code and the implementation details at https://github.com/bhattarailab/Surgical-Vision-World-Model.

papers.title: Learning Implicit Solves for Dynamic Simulations
papers.abstract: High-fidelity simulation of dynamical systems is central to scientific discovery and engineering design, yet remains computationally demanding. Here we introduce the Implicit Neural Operator Solver (INOS), which learns the implicit solve and encodes a time integrator. INOS pretrains a neural operator from static equilibrium solutions and reuses it within Newmark-$β$ integration. At each time increment, the integrator forms an effective equilibrium problem, the pretrained neural operator infers the next-step solution field, and the Newmark relations advance the dynamic state. Numerical examples in linear and nonlinear elastodynamics demonstrate accurate full-field predictions without dynamic trajectory supervision. Comparative results show that INOS, evaluated zero-shot, achieves higher predictive accuracy than neural solver baselines trained on dynamic simulations. In addition, INOS delivers over 4,600$\times$ speedup in nonlinear simulations over sequential classical finite-element solvers. INOS natively accommodates changes in dynamic conditions and enables reuse of the pretrained operator across spatial and temporal discretizations. Further evaluation demonstrates a stable million-step rollout. These findings establish INOS as a reusable neural implicit solver for accurate, efficient, and robust dynamic modeling.

papers.title: Development of Highly Printable GelMA/Laponite Bioinks by a Rheology-Guided Design Strategy: Impact of the GelMA Synthetic Procedure
papers.abstract: Gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) is the most widely used biomaterial for extrusion-based bioprinting. However, its intrinsic rheological properties often require optimisation with rheological modifiers, such as the nanoclay Laponite (Lapo). Since the rheological behaviour of GelMA/Lapo hybrid bioinks depends on polymer–nanoclay interactions, the physicochemical and conformational properties of GelMA are expected to critically influence Lapo incorporation, the resulting rheological behaviour, and ultimately printability. Accordingly, this study combines formulation design with a systematic rheology-guided screening strategy. Two GelMA derivatives (GelMADP and GelMASP) obtained through different synthesis procedures, and characterised by distinct physicochemical and structural properties, were used to prepare GelMA/Lapo bioinks under physiologically relevant conditions. GelMASP enabled homogeneous incorporation of higher Lapo contents than GelMADP, expanding the formulation space and allowing the development of hybrid inks with improved rheological properties. A sequential rheological roadmap integrating oscillation temperature-ramp, flow-sweep, yield stress, and elastic recovery analyses was then used to progressively screen the formulations and guide the selection of suitable processing conditions. Among the investigated formulations, SP20-3 (20% w/v GelMASP and 3% w/v Lapo) exhibited the most suitable rheological profile, combining favourable temperature-dependent gelation, pronounced shear-thinning behaviour, and rapid structural recovery, ultimately leading to high printing fidelity. These properties were largely retained also after high-density cell inclusion. Overall, these results identify the physicochemical and conformational properties of the starting GelMA as critical design parameters governing polymer–clay network organisation, rheological behaviour, and bioink printability, while highlighting the value of a systematic rheology-guided approach for formulation screening and optimisation.

papers.title: Strategically tuning oxygen in multiple phases for high-performance titanium alloys
papers.abstract: Oxygen is traditionally detrimental to ductility in titanium alloys. Recent advances have reframed oxygen as a design tool for forming beneficial microstructures and enhancing performance. Yet, its role has been mostly limited to the α phase in dual-phase α-β titanium alloys. Introducing sufficient oxygen into β when both phases coexist may unlock beneficial motifs and improve performance. We present that strategic oxygen partitioning across coexisting α and β phases enables substantial oxygen in β and triggers a β → O' phase transformation via atomic rearrangements. This O' phase acts as a precursor for stress-induced martensitic transformation (O'→α") during deformation, activating synergistic transformation-induced and twinning-induced plasticity. The resulting α-β-O' titanium alloy (Ti-6Al-4V-0.39O) achieves an ultimate tensile strength of 1200 ± 30 MPa, ductility of 23.5 ± 1.5%, and a strength-and-strain product of 28.2 GPa·%. Our work establishes a general principle for strategically tuning oxygen in titanium alloy design and demonstrates potential for recycling oxygen-contaminated titanium waste. This study utilizes oxygen-rich Ti powders for additive manufacturing and establishes a method for strategically tuning oxygen in multiple phases in high-performance titanium alloy design which strengthens Ti-alloys with oxygen, rather than embrittling them.

papers.title: Educational impedance and its importance in the context of teaching and learning: an analogy with electrical impedance
papers.abstract: This paper develops the concept of educational impedance as a metaphorical framework for interpreting barriers in teaching and learning through an analogy with electrical impedance. Drawing on a synthesis of literature from education and electrical engineering, the framework distinguishes resistance, defined as learner-related barriers to participation and understanding, from reactance, defined as misalignment between instructional strategies and learners' cognitive, motivational, or contextual characteristics. Educational impedance denotes the combined influence of these dimensions, whereas impedance matching refers to the continuous adaptation of instruction to learners’ needs. The framework is used to organize conceptual relationships among prior knowledge, engagement, instructional design, and formative feedback. Hypothetical classroom examples illustrate how these relationships might inform pedagogical reflection and instructional planning. Active learning, scaffolding, and feedback are discussed as possible strategies for addressing identified barriers, rather than as interventions whose effectiveness is established by the proposed framework. The contribution is an integrative conceptual lens, not a validated measurement instrument or predictive model. Whether its application improves engagement, knowledge retention, or academic performance remains a question for future empirical investigation.

papers.title: Lecture-based teaching in medical education: reform is the need of time.
papers.abstract: Objective: To assess medical students’ perceptions of lecture-based teaching and the need for modification of traditional lectures with more effective instructional strategies. Study Design: Cross-sectional mixed method study. Setting: MBBS Students of Nishtar Medical University, Pakistan. Period: May 2025- July 2025. Methods: 374 MBBS students were given hard copy of a structured questionnaire to explore students’ perceptions of lecture-based teaching and active learning methods. It consisted of biodata, 15 close ended and two open ended questions. Responses were measured on a three-point Likert scale ranging from disagree to agree. Quantitative data were analyzed using SPSS version 26. Descriptive statistical measures, including frequencies and percentages were computed to summarize the data. Qualitative data were examined through thematic analysis. Results: 340 students returned the filled questionnaire. The vast majority (85.3%) agreed that the lectures are helpful for understanding the fundamental concepts related to medical education and this is complemented by audio-visual aids used during delivery of lectures. Majority were of the opinion that the lecture-based teaching mainly promotes passive learning. However, a greater number agreed that the inclusion of interactive components improves engagement during lectures. About 71.5% students commented that the attention tends to decline during 45-60 minutes lecture duration. Conclusion: Lectures continue to play a vital role in medical education but require modernization to meet evolving learner needs. Emphasizing interactivity, clarity, and integration with active learning strategies can optimize their effectiveness and relevance in contemporary medical curricula.

papers.abstract: To address the challenge of balancing point forecast accuracy with the quantification of probabilistic uncertainty in short-term traffic flow forecasting, we propose a probabilistic traffic flow forecasting model, AT-BiLSTM-STHGPR, based on attention-based bidirectional long-short-term memory (BiLSTM) and spatiotemporal heteroscedastic Gaussian process regression (STHGPR).The model consists of three modules: temporal feature extraction, deep feature fusion, and probabilistic forecasting.Point prediction and probabilistic prediction experiments were conducted on the PEMS04 and PEMS08 public traffic datasets, and ablation experiments were designed to validate the effectiveness of each module.The experimental results show that, compared to baseline models such as MC-Dropout, DeepAR, and Attention-BiLSTM, this model achieves superior results across evaluation metrics including MAE, RMSE, CRPS, and MIS.Ablation experiments confirm that the attention mechanism, the feature fusion module, and spatiotemporal heteroscedastic Gaussian process regression all contribute to positive performance gains.

papers.title: Reverse Haptic Alerting: Human‐Centered Intelligent Systems That Turn Chemical and Biomedical Signals Into Felt Cues
papers.abstract: Wearable chemical and biomedical sensors have advanced rapidly, yet most still communicate through color change, an electrical readout, or a smartphone alert. These channels can become unreliable precisely when they are needed most: Under personal protective equipment (PPE), in noise, or during cognitive overload. This Perspective argues for inverting the usual information flow. Instead of converting touch into data, as tactile sensors and electronic skins do, it converts a chemical or biological signal into a stimulus felt through skin mechanoreceptors. The field is framed as an intelligent, human‐centered sensing architecture along three axes: the target signal (from sweat biomarkers to chemical‐warfare agents (CWAs)), the stimuli‐responsive transduction mechanism, and the body site at which the cue is perceived. Because tactile acuity varies more than tenfold across the body, placement is treated as a primary design variable. A machine‐learning (ML) layer is then proposed that builds a personalized digital twin of the wearer’s tactile perception and, in a closed loop, recommends where to place a sensor and how to actuate it, raising detection while keeping stimulus, discomfort, and false alarms low. An illustrative synthetic case study demonstrates the detection–discomfort trade‐off, and the required datasets and experiments are outlined.

papers.title: Inverse identification of the consolidation coefficient in cyclic poroelastic consolidation using physics-informed neural networks
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of the consolidation coefficient is essential for predicting pore pressure and settlement in cyclically loaded saturated soils, yet remains challenging due to sparse and noisy field data. While Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) excel in solving inverse problems, their application in coupled cyclic poroelastic consolidation remains limited. This study develops a PINN framework for both forward simulation of consolidation and inverse estimation of the consolidation coefficient under haversine loading. Results demonstrate that the forward PINN accurately captures the coupled consolidation response by reproducing both pore pressure dissipation and settlement evolution. In the inverse problem, the model successfully identifies the consolidation coefficient while simultaneously reconstructing pore pressure and displacement fields. Pore pressure observations are found to be more informative than displacement data; for the one-dimensional (1D) homogeneous case and sensor configurations considered, errors below 5% are obtained when at least two pore pressure sensors are used. The model also performs reliably using only early-cycle observations and remains robust under moderate uncertainty for the measurement configurations investigated. Parameter identification is robust to pore-pressure noise but sensitive to displacement noise. These results demonstrate the potential of PINNs as a data-efficient framework for cyclic consolidation problems within the scope of the adopted 1D model.

papers.title: Edge AI Imitation of Event-Triggered Model Predictive Control for an Inverted Pendulum
papers.abstract: Event-triggered model predictive control (MPC) updates the control input only when needed, but it still solves an optimization problem at every event, which on the studied cart–pole can exceed its 10 ms control period. We propose a compact multi-task neural network that replaces the whole scheme: it decides when to update the input and which value to apply, using only online measurements. It is trained on 500 physical recordings, adapted to a simulated teacher and refined with DAgger. Feeding it the held input produces a copycat policy that is accurate in open loop but sluggish in closed loop; in a matched comparison over four training seeds, removing that input raises full-episode success from three to 39 of 40 episodes. In simulation, at the default sensor noise, the final network completes all swing-up and tracking episodes, with time to upright and tracking error close to the teacher’s, whereas on the simulated teacher, tree ensembles have 1.4–1.6 times its open-loop error. In an open-loop replay on an ESP32-S3 microcontroller, a step takes under 40% of the period. In tracking and full episodes, it updates the input 33–39% more often than the teacher, mainly because it does not learn the rule’s sparsity.

papers.title: Uncertainty quantification and global sensitivity analysis of a thermally coupled hydrodynamic journal bearing
papers.abstract: A deterministic bearing calculation gives one value per performance measure, although its inputs are uncertain. This paper attributes that uncertainty for one bearing class: a plain journal bearing with L / D = 0.5 and ISO VG 46 oil, at two reference duty points and across a twelve-point duty sweep. The finite-width Reynolds equation with the Guembel condition is coupled to a Walther viscosity–temperature law and a global energy balance, and a similarity-based operator solves it in about 30 μs. Against published experiments, the predicted eccentricity agrees within 0.012 between 4 and 10 kN at 2000 rpm, whereas the maximum temperature is underpredicted. Eight documented uncertain inputs are propagated by Monte Carlo and Latin hypercube sampling and decomposed with Sobol indices. At heavy duty the supply temperature explains 67% of the variance of the minimum film thickness and 73% of that of the friction power loss; the load explains 80% of that of the peak pressure. Interactions are weak. The roughness share of the film-parameter variance (65%) is largely definitional. The local clearance elasticity of the film thickness changes sign at a nominal eccentricity ratio of 0.64, and the clearance index falls from 0.51 to a minimum of 0.002. From 10 7 runs, a nominal film parameter of 6.0, twice the full-film limit, still leaves a mixed-lubrication probability of 2.51 × 10 −3 . The leading input changes only if the supply-temperature standard deviation falls below about 3 K, whereas absolute probabilities depend on the input model and thermal closure.

papers.title: Bayesian Neural Networks for Uncertainty‑Aware Toxicity Prediction of Metallic Nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Nanoparticle cytotoxicity prediction remains challenging due to the complex interplay of physicochemical properties and experimental conditions, compounded by the critical need for uncertainty quantification in safety assessments. Here, we present a hybrid computational framework integrating Quantitative Structure-Activity Relationship (QSAR) feature engineering with Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs) to predict metallic nanoparticle toxicity while explicitly quantifying predictive uncertainty. Using a curated dataset of 1,363 experimental records (25 nanoparticle formulations) from multiple in vitro studies, with every model evaluated on formulations unseen during training, we implemented a three-stage pipeline: (i) domain-guided preprocessing with multicollinearity assessment, (ii) benchmarking of deterministic classifiers (Random Forest, SVM, Multi-Layer Perceptron and three simpler models), and (iii) variational Bayesian inference for probabilistic classification. In repeated formulation-grouped cross-validation Random Forest discriminated best (ROC-AUC = 0.974), followed by logistic regression (0.967), which was better calibrated on held-out formulations (ECE 0.046 versus 0.130). The BNN discriminated well (ROC-AUC = 0.979) but underestimated toxicity at the 0.5 threshold (recall 0.520), while providing individual prediction uncertainty estimates from the variational posterior. Predictive uncertainty identified most misclassified predictions (AUROC = 0.92) but did not rise for samples outside the training descriptor space, which were detected by leverage. Dual-criterion applicability domain filtering (leverage and uncertainty thresholds) retained 44.2% of test samples (52 of the 125 toxic ones), achieving 0.942 recall and a 0.058 false negative rate, and flagged the remaining 55.8% for confirmatory testing. Impact statement: uncertainty-aware models evaluated on unseen formulations can separate nanoparticle cytotoxicity predictions usable for screening from those that require confirmatory testing.

summary_en.motivation: Reliable safety screening of metallic nanoparticles requires predictive models that also quantify uncertainty rather than issuing point predictions.

papers.title: TECHNOLOGY OF FORMING A BLOCK OF PROBLEM-BASED CASES AND PRACTICAL PRODUCTION TASKS IN EDUCATIONAL LITERATURE
papers.abstract: This article examines the methodologies and technological approaches for designing and integrating problem-based cases and practical production tasks within modern educational literature, specifically tailored for higher and professional education. The paradigm shift toward competence-based education requires a structural transformation of textbooks from passive information carriers into active learning simulators. The author develops a structured multi-stage algorithm for case integration and classifies production tasks into three hierarchical levels: Technological-Reproductive, Analytical-Tactical, and Strategic-Creative. A complete systemic matrix is provided to guide textbook authors and curriculum designers. The practical implementation of this technology ensures the minimization of the gap between academic theory and actual industrial requirements, enhancing graduates' professional adaptability and critical thinking skills.

papers.title: Stable Combustion of Ultra-Low-Concentration Methane in a Dual-Channel Counterflow D-TPMS Porous Burner: A Pore-Scale Numerical Study
papers.abstract: At ultra-low methane concentrations, limited heat release makes it difficult to preheat the incoming mixture sufficiently to sustain stable combustion. This study employs three-dimensional pore-scale simulations to investigate a porous burner based on a Diamond-type triply periodic minimal surface (D-TPMS). The burner comprises two interpenetrating flow-channel networks separated by a solid wall, allowing co-current operation with both streams flowing in the same direction or counterflow operation with the streams flowing in opposite directions. Under counterflow operation, fresh methane–air mixtures enter the two channels simultaneously from opposite ends of the burner and undergo preheating and combustion within their respective channels. Hot combustion products in each channel transfer heat through the separating wall to the incoming mixture in the adjacent channel, enabling continuous mutual heat recovery without direct mixing or periodic flow reversal. Under co-current operation, stable combustion of a mixture containing 4.0 vol.% CH4 was maintained at an inlet velocity of 0.10 m s−1, whereas flame blow-off occurred at 0.15 m s−1. In contrast, under counterflow operation, a 48 mm D-TPMS medium sustained stable combustion at 0.40 m s−1 with methane concentrations as low as 1.6 vol.%. At the same inlet velocity, increasing the medium length to 98 mm provided a longer axial region for inter-channel heat exchange, and stable combustion was sustained at methane concentrations as low as 1.0 vol.%. These findings indicate that continuous mutual heat recovery enabled by counterflow operation within the dual-channel D-TPMS structure substantially extends the stable operating range of ultra-low-concentration methane combustion.

papers.title: The Influence of a Teacher's Classical Teaching Style on Student Learning Engagement in Grade V Elementary School Classes
papers.abstract: Active learning is one of the important aspects in learning Christian Religious Education (PAK). Students are not only expected to listen to the teacher's explanation, but also to be involved in learning activities, such as doing assignments, asking questions, expressing opinions, and seeking information. In this case, the classical teaching style places the teacher as the center of material delivery so that student involvement needs attention. This study aims to determine the influence of teachers' classical teaching style on student learning activity in PAK learning in grade V of SDN 4 Palangka and measure the magnitude of this influence. This study uses a quantitative approach with a non-experimental design. Respondents of the research were students in grade V of SDN 4 Palangka. Data were collected through a Likert scale questionnaire and documentation. Furthermore, data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, residual normality test, simple linear regression, t-test, and determination coefficient with the help of IBM SPSS Statistics 27. The results showed that the teacher's classical teaching style obtained an average score of 3.88 per item, while the student's learning activity obtained an average score of 3.86 per item. Both variables are included in the high category. The results of the t-test showed a calculated t-value of 5.871 with a significance value of less than 0.001. These results show that the teacher's classical teaching style has a positive and significant statistical influence on student learning activity. Meanwhile, the determination coefficient value (R Square) of 0.552 shows that the regression model is able to explain 55.2% of the variation in student learning activity scores. The remaining 44.8% cannot be explained by this research model. Thus, there is a positive and significant predictive relationship between teachers' classical teaching styles and students' learning activity in PAK learning in grade V of SDN 4 Palangka.

papers.title: Effect of heat treatment on the tensile and flexural properties of PLA and ABS after 3D printing
papers.abstract: This study examines the collective influence of infill densities and post-printing heat treatment on the tensile and flexural performance of Fused Filament Fabrication (FFF) printed polylactic acid (PLA) and acrylonitrile butadiene styrene (ABS) with a gyroid internal architecture. Attention is given to the effect of heating rate relative to the glass transition temperature (Tg) of each polymer. PLA and ABS specimen were printed at three infill densities (20%, 65%, and 95%). The samples were subjected to non-heat-treated (NHT), direct heat treatment (DHT), and gradual heat treatment (GHT) conditions. Heat treatment was performed at 60°C for PLA and 100°C for ABS. Tensile and three-point bending tests were accomplished using a Universal Testing Machine. Fracture morphology was analysed using scanning electron microscopy to relate mechanical response to failure characteristics. Crystallinity and glass transition behaviour were characterised using XRD and DSC. Tensile peak load increased with infill density for both materials. For PLA, both DHT and GHT reduced tensile and flexural peak loads by approximately 6-16%, which may be associated with stress relaxation and localised softening near its Tg. For ABS, DHT resulted in consistent tensile improvement (4-5%), while GHT produced significant improvements in flexural peak load (23-43%). Fracture analysis showed improved inter-ligament bonding in ABS after heat treatment, while PLA exhibited localised softening of the internal structure. Unlike prior studies that examined heat treatment of PLA or ABS independently, this study directly compares DHT and GHT under identical gyroid architecture and loading modes for both materials simultaneously. The results show that heating rate and treatment temperature compared to Tg influence mechanical performance differently in PLA and ABS, highlighting the material-specific interaction between infill density and heat treatment.

papers.title: Hierarchical nonlinear MPC and super-twisting sliding mode control for a wheeled biped robot under uncertainties
papers.abstract: This paper presents a hierarchical control framework integrating Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) with Super-Twisting Sliding Mode Control (STSMC) for wheeled bipedal robots. While these platforms offer both wheeled efficiency and legged versatility, their unstable underactuated dynamics and sensitivity to modeling errors pose significant control challenges. The proposed three-layer architecture employs a high-level NMPC for trajectory generation, a higher-frequency STSMC for robust tracking with finite-time convergence, and Whole-Body Control for wrench-to-torque mapping. Simulation results on the 8-DoF Tron-1A platform demonstrate superior disturbance rejection: the framework recovers from 100 N lateral impulses that destabilize baseline NMPC, reduces orientation errors by up to 80% on rough terrain with 0.1 m elevation changes, and eliminates steady-state errors under 20% actuator degradation with joint friction. These results validate the hierarchical NMPC-STSMC architecture for achieving robust wheeled bipedal locomotion under significant model uncertainty and external perturbations.
